Here is my comprehensive report of all code related to jumping, spacebar input, and jump delay in the codebase.

---

## Summary

This is a Minecraft modding project (MCP/Mod Coder Pack) with OptiFine integration. The codebase is a decompiled version of Minecraft's source code. There is **no custom "jump delay" or "jump cooldown" mechanism** beyond the vanilla Minecraft `jumpTicks` field. The spacebar (key code 57) is the default jump key.

---

## 1. Spacebar / Jump Key Binding

**File:** `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\src\main\java\net\minecraft\client\settings\GameSettings.java`
- **Line 140:** The jump key is bound to key code **57** (Spacebar):
```java
public KeyBinding keyBindJump = new KeyBinding("key.jump", 57, "key.categories.movement");
```

---

## 2. Movement Input (Reading the Spacebar)

**File:** `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\src\main\java\net\minecraft\util\MovementInput.java`
- **Line 7:** The `jump` boolean field:
```java
public boolean jump;
```

**File:** `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\src\main\java\net\minecraft\util\MovementInputFromOptions.java`
- **Line 39:** Reads the spacebar state directly each tick:
```java
this.jump = this.gameSettings.keyBindJump.isKeyDown();
```

---

## 3. The Jump Delay Mechanism (`jumpTicks`)

**File:** `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\src\main\java\net\minecraft\entity\EntityLivingBase.java`

- **Line 111:** The jump delay field declaration:
```java
private int jumpTicks;
```

- **Lines 1686-1689:** Decrements `jumpTicks` each tick in `onLivingUpdate()`:
```java
if (this.jumpTicks > 0)
{
    --this.jumpTicks;
}
```

- **Lines 1744-1763:** The core jump logic -- jump only fires when `jumpTicks == 0`, then sets it to **10**:
```java
if (this.isJumping)
{
    if (this.isInWater())
    {
        this.updateAITick();
    }
    else if (this.isInLava())
    {
        this.handleJumpLava();
    }
    else if (this.onGround && this.jumpTicks == 0)
    {
        this.jump();
        this.jumpTicks = 10;
    }
}
else
{
    this.jumpTicks = 0;
}
```

This means there is a **10-tick cooldown** (0.5 seconds at 20 TPS) between jumps when holding the spacebar.

## 4. The `jump()` Method (Actual Jump Execution)

**File:** `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\src\main\java\net\minecraft\entity\EntityLivingBase.java`

```java
{

protected void jump()
{
    this.motionY = (double)this.getJumpUpwardsMotion();

    if (this.isPotionActive(Potion.jump))

        this.motionY += (double)((float)(this.getActivePotionEffect(Potion.jump).getAmplifier() + 1) * 0.1F);
    }

    if (this.isSprinting())
    {
        float f = this.rotationYaw * 0.017453292F;
        this.motionX -= (double)(MathHelper.sin(f) * 0.2F);
        this.motionZ += (double)(MathHelper.cos(f) * 0.2F);

}
```

metadata.displayText: which is better? just java or kotlin

messages.text: which is better? just java or kotlin

content.text:
The user is asking whether Java or Kotlin is better for their MCP (Minecraft Coder Pack) base project. This is a general programming question about which language to use for Minecraft modding/client development.

For Minecraft 1.8.9 MCP development:
- Java is the native language of Minecraft and MCP
- Kotlin can be used but requires additional setup and may have compatibility issues
- Most MCP bases, tutorials, and examples are in Java
- The decompiled Minecraft source is in Java

I should give a practical recommendation based on their use case.

For MCP 1.8.9 development, **Java** is the better choice. Here's why:

### Java (Recommended)
- **Native to Minecraft** — the decompiled source is in Java, so everything maps 1:1
- **No extra setup** — works out of the box with Gradle MCP bases
- **All tutorials/examples** — every MCP guide, forum post, and base uses Java
- **Better compatibility** — no issues with LWJGL, reflection, or obfuscation
- **Easier to debug** — stack traces match the decompiled code exactly

### Kotlin
- Requires adding Kotlin plugin and stdlib to `build.gradle`
- Can cause issues with Minecraft's reflection and obfuscation
- Harder to follow MCP tutorials (you'd need to mentally translate Java → Kotlin)
- Slightly more verbose build configuration

### Bottom line
Stick with **Java** for MCP bases. Kotlin is great for general Android/backend development, but for Minecraft 1.8.9 modding, Java is the standard and will save you a lot of headaches.

## Objective
Modify a Minecraft 1.8.9 MCP base client (jump mechanics), then get it building and launching via TLauncher; a ViaMCP integration attempt was started and then rolled back.

## Requirements
- Remove jump cooldown when holding spacebar
- Build the client with Gradle per README
- Generate launcher `.json` so the client starts
- User then said "remove any last viaMCP code in gradle" (gradle only — source files not yet removed)

## Decisions
- Vanilla `jumpTicks` is the only jump-delay mechanism; set post-jump value to `0` instead of `10`
- Launcher JSON should use `"inheritsFrom": "1.8.9"` (vanilla 1.8.9 must be installed) instead of a full manual library list
- `mainClass` is `Start`; ViaMCP/ViaVersion integration abandoned (API incompatible with all available ViaVersion 4.x versions)
- Java recommended over Kotlin for MCP work

## Work State

### Completed
- Jump delay removed in `EntityLivingBase.java` (`jumpTicks = 0`)
- `Cartesian.java` compile error fixed (restructured `Product.iterator()` ternary into if/else with type witness)
- Successful build produced `build/libs/GradleMCP-Base-1.8.9.jar` (~10.4 MB)
- `GradleMCP.json` created with `inheritsFrom: 1.8.9`, `mainClass: Start`, launchwrapper + asm-all
- `Start.java` simplified to `Main.main(args);` — fixes `MultipleArgumentsForOptionException` for `--version`, `--userProperties`, `--assetsDir`, `--assetIndex`, `--accessToken`
- `build.gradle` reverted to original (ViaVersion repo + deps removed)

### Active
(none)

### Blocked
- Client launch is unverified. Last known error was `java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: Can't load library: C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Roaming\.tlauncher\legacy\Minecraft\game\..\natives\windows\lwjgl64.dll` at `net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(Main.java:39)` — natives never found; removing the hardcoded librarypath from `Start.java` has not been retested.
- **Project will not compile as-is**: ViaMCP sources were moved from `src/de` to `src/main/java/de` and still fail with `package com.viaversion.viaversion.api does not exist`, `com.viaversion.viaversion.protocol.version.BaseVersionProvider`, `com.viaversion.viabackwards.protocol.v1_17to1_16_4`, `com.viaversion.viaversion.protocols.v1_16_1to1_16_2.packet`.

## Next Move
1. Delete `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\src\main\java\de` to fully remove ViaMCP (gradle was already reverted).
2. Re-run build to confirm green: `cd C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase; ./gradlew build` (PowerShell: use `;`, not `&&`).
3. Copy jar to `versions/GradleMCP-1.8.9/GradleMCP-1.8.9.jar` and verify natives still load; if not, inspect TLauncher natives extraction / set `org.lwjgl.librarypath` to the actual natives dir.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/entity/EntityLivingBase.java`: jump block at ~line 1754, `jumpTicks = 0` is the jump-delay fix
- `src/main/java/Start.java`: entry point, now just `Main.main(args);`; also has unused `concat()` helper
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/util/Cartesian.java`: locally patched to compile under newer JDK
- `GradleMCP.json`: launcher version manifest at project root
- `build.gradle`: reverted to original deps/repos
- `src/main/java/de/florianmichael/...`: leftover ViaMCP source that breaks the build
- `README.md`: build instructions (build task → `build/libs` → delete `META-INF` from jar)
- `C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Roaming\.tlauncher\legacy\Minecraft\`: launcher game dir (natives not found here)

## Important Context
- Build command on Windows PowerShell: `cd C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase; ./gradlew build` (uses `gradlew`, not `gradle`)
- All changes are uncommitted; nothing was committed or pushed
- Warnings about deprecated `new Integer(...)`/`new Float(...)` in `EntityMinecart.java` are pre-existing and non-fatal
- Runs on Java 21 under TLauncher; `natives/windows/lwjgl64.dll` is required

## The 12 mixins and what each one does

| Mixin | Target | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `MixinItemRenderer` | `ItemRenderer` | 1.7 bow pullback, 1.7 first-person item transform, swing-progress override, punch-while-using block-hitting, item-switch freeze |
| `MixinEntityRenderer` | `EntityRenderer` | Replace `getEyeHeight()` in `orientCamera` + `renderWorldDirections` with `SneakHandler` |
| `MixinMinecraft` | `Minecraft` | `rightClickMouse` → `resetBlockRemoving()` so punching doesn't break the block |
| `LayerArmorBaseMixin` | `LayerArmorBase` | `shouldCombineTextures()` → `true` (red armor on hit) |
| `GuiIngameForgeMixin` | Forge's `GuiIngameForge` | Kill F3 debug-screen boxes/shadow, kill health-bar flash |
| `MixinGuiPlayerTabOverlay` | `GuiPlayerTabOverlay` | Disable tab icons |
| `MixinOnlineIndicator` | Essential `OnlineIndicator` | Remove Essential tab indicator (`@Pseudo`, Essential-only) |

| `ModelBipedMixin` | `ModelBiped` | `@ModifyConstant(-0.5235988F)` → `0` in `setRotationAngles` |
| `RenderFishMixin` | `RenderFish` | 1.7 fishing-line offset |
| `RenderManagerMixin` | `RenderManager` | Remove F3+B eye line/box |
| `ItemFoodAccessor` | `ItemFood` | `@Accessor` for `alwaysEdible` |

## Why it can't be dropped in as-is

Three hard dependencies an MCP base doesn't have:
1. **Forge** — `net.minecraftforge.fml.*`, `MinecraftForge.EVENT_BUS`, `GuiIngameForge`
2. **Sponge Mixin** — the entire patch mechanism3. **Essential API** — `gg.essential.vigilance.Vigilant` (config GUI/TOML), `gg.essential.api.commands.Command`, `OnlineIndicator`

## The port plan for MCP

Since we own the source, every mixin becomes a **direct edit** — no Mixin, no Forge, no Essential:

| Mixin | Becomes |
|---|---|
| `AnimationHandler`, `SneakHandler`, `FishingLineHandler` | New plain classes, ticking from `Minecraft.runTick()` |
| `OldAnimationsSettings` | `public static boolean` toggles (drop Vigilance/TOML) |
| `MixinItemRenderer` | Edits in `ItemRenderer.java` (`doBowTransformations`, `renderItemInFirstPerson`, `updateEquippedItem`) |
| `MixinEntityRenderer` | Edit `EntityRenderer.orientCamera` / `renderWorldDirections` |
| `MixinMinecraft` | Edit `Minecraft.rightClickMouse()` |
| `LayerArmorBaseMixin` | Edit `LayerArmorBase.shouldCombineTextures()` |
| `GuiIngameForgeMixin` | Edit vanilla `GuiIngame` (line 591 `flag` + debug-text draw) |
| `MixinGuiPlayerTabOverlay` | Edit `GuiPlayerTabOverlay.renderPlayerlist` |
| `MixinOnlineIndicator` | **Drop** — Essential-only, we don't have it |
| `MixinRenderItem` | Edit `RenderItem.renderItemModelTransform` |
| `ModelBipedMixin` | `ModelBiped.java:145` `-0.5235988F` → `0` |
| `RenderFishMixin` | Edit `RenderFish.doRender` (`new Vec3(-0.36D, 0.03D, 0.35D)`) |

## Objective
- Integrate the Sk1er "Old Animations" mod (`C:\Users\dinhv\Downloads\OldAnimations-master.zip`) into the existing Minecraft 1.8.9 MCP base client; user has repeatedly asked to "read all this project" (i.e., fully understand the mod's source before porting).

## Requirements
- Port the mod into an MCP base — the original uses Forge `@Mod`/`@EventHandler`, SpongePowered Mixins, and Essential API (Vigilance config, `EssentialAPI`, mixinextras `ModifyExpressionValue`/`WrapWithCondition`), none of which exist in a plain MCP client; must be converted to direct source edits / MCP-compatible code
- Read all of the mod's project first (user repeated this request ~6 times)
- Earlier requirements still standing: remove jump cooldown when holding spacebar; remove leftover ViaMCP code from gradle (done) and source (not done)

## Decisions
- Convert Forge/Mixin/Essential-dependent code into plain MCP source rather than adding those frameworks
- Vanilla `jumpTicks` is the only jump-delay mechanism; set post-jump value to `0` instead of `10`
- Launcher JSON uses `"inheritsFrom": "1.8.9"` (vanilla 1.8.9 must be installed) instead of a manual library list
- `mainClass` is `Start`; `Start.java` simplified to `Main.main(args)` to avoid `MultipleArgumentsForOptionException`
- ViaMCP/ViaVersion integration abandoned (API incompatible with all available ViaVersion 4.x versions)
- Java (not Kotlin) preferred for MCP work

The port is complete and builds clean from scratch.

## What I did

Ported Sk1er Old Animations into the MCP base by replacing all three of its framework dependencies with direct source edits:

| Original (Forge / Mixin / Essential) | Now |
|---|---|
| 12 mixins across `mixins/` | Direct edits to 9 vanilla classes |
| `Vigilant` config + TOML | `OldAnimationsSettings` static booleans + `/oldanimations` chat command |
| `MinecraftForge.EVENT_BUS` / `TickEvent` | `OldAnimations.onClientTick()` from `Minecraft.runTick()` |
| `gg.essential` `OnlineIndicator` mixin | **Dropped** — Essential-only, not applicable |
| `ItemFoodAccessor` `@Accessor` | Added `ItemFood.getAlwaysEdible()` |

**New package** `src/main/java/net/minecraft/oldanimations/`: `OldAnimations` (tick + chat entry), `AnimationHandler`, `SneakHandler`, `FishingLineHandler`, `OldAnimationsSettings` (16 toggles), `OldAnimationsCommand`.

**Edited**: `ItemRenderer` (bow, 1.7 item matrix, swing progress, punching, item-switch freeze), `EntityRenderer` (sneak eye height), `Minecraft` (tick + `resetBlockRemoving`), `ModelBiped` (`-0.5235988F`), `RenderItem` (3rd-person block), `RenderFish`, `RenderManager`, `LayerArmorBase`, `GuiOverlayDebug`, `GuiIngame`, `GuiPlayerTabOverlay`, `GuiScreen`, `ItemFood`.

## Verification

- `./gradlew clean build` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**, jar at `build/libs/GradleMCP-Base-1.8.9.jar` (10.9 MB)
- Wrote and ran a throwaway test harness against the built jar covering the command parser: **all 40+ assertions pass** (defaults match upstream, `/oam` alias, non-commands pass through, bad input never mutates state). Test files deleted afterwards.

## Two bugs I caught while porting

Worth flagging, since both were mine and both silently disabled features:

1. **I dropped transforms from the 1.7 item matrix** — I initially wrote `translate(0.028, 0.15, -0.05)` instead of the real `translate(0.588, 0.37, -0.77)` + `translate(0, -0.3, 0)` + `rotate(50°,...)` + `scale(-2, 2, -2)`. Caught by re-reading `AnimationHandler.java`.
2. **`oldBow`/`oldEating`/`oldSwordBlock` were ignored** — I computed an `enabled` flag in a switch but then never read it, so the 1.7 transform applied regardless of those settings. Caught reviewing the diff.

I also corrected two injection points to match the mixins exactly: `RenderItem` had to apply at the `renderItem(stack, model)` call (after the baked transform), not at method head, and the fishing-rod case had to fall through to the 1.7 placement even when `oldRod` is off.

## Per your choices- **Chat-command toggles**: `/oldanimations list`, `/oldanimations <name> on|off`, `/oldanimations all on|off` (plus `/oam`). Settings are discovered reflectively, so adding a toggle only means adding a boolean.
- **Camera everywhere**: sneak eye height applied in both `orientCamera` (which also drives the third-person camera and its block-intersection test) and `renderWorldDirections`.
- Defaults are identical to upstream, including `oldTab = false`.

Nothing is committed. Note the client still hasn't been launched — the TLauncher natives issue (`lwjgl64.dll`) from earlier is unresolved, so the visuals are unverified at runtime.

## Objective
Port the Sk1er "Old Animations" mod (`C:\Users\dinhv\Downloads\OldAnimations-master.zip`, extracted to temp) into the existing Minecraft 1.8.9 MCP base client as direct source edits, since the original relies on Forge, Sponge Mixins, and Essential API which don't exist in a plain MCP client.

## Requirements
- Port the mod into the MCP base by converting Forge/Mixin/Essential code into plain MCP source — do NOT add those frameworks
- Read the entire mod project before porting (user requested this repeatedly, ~6 times)
- Settings via chat-command toggles (user's explicit choice over static booleans/config file)
- Sneak eye-height change applies to camera everywhere (first-person, third-person camera, world directions) — user's explicit choice
- Verify with `./gradlew build` (user's explicit choice)
- Earlier standing: remove jump cooldown when holding spacebar (done); remove leftover ViaMCP code from gradle (done) and source (done)

## Decisions
- Every mixin became a direct source edit; `MixinOnlineIndicator` dropped entirely (Essential-only)
- `Vigilant` config replaced by `OldAnimationsSettings` static booleans + `/oldanimations` chat command; settings discovered reflectively so adding a toggle only requires adding a boolean
- Chat command hooked into `GuiScreen.sendChatMessage(String, boolean)` (returns true = consume, don't send to server)
- Tick hooked via `OldAnimations.onClientTick()` from `Minecraft.runTick()` in its own `"oldAnimations"` profiler section, gated on `!isGamePaused`
- The F3 debug overlay is `GuiOverlayDebug` (NOT chat) — an earlier attempt routed it through `ChatComponentText`/`GuiNewChat` and was reverted
- `ItemFood.alwaysEdible` exposed via new `getAlwaysEdible()` rather than an `@Accessor` mixin
- `Start.java` simplified to `Main.main(args)` (unused `concat()` helper removed)
- ViaMCP/ViaVersion integration abandoned earlier (API incompatible with all ViaVersion 4.x)

## Work State
### Completed
- Full read of every file in the OldAnimations project (12 mixins, 3 handlers, config, command, resources, gradle files)
- Removed leftover ViaMCP sources at `src/main/java/de/` — build baseline green
- Jump delay removed in `EntityLivingBase.java` (`jumpTicks = 0`)
- `Cartesian.java` compile error fixed for newer JDK
- Created new package `src/main/java/net/minecraft/oldanimations/`: `OldAnimations`, `OldAnimationsSettings`, `AnimationHandler`, `SneakHandler`, `FishingLineHandler`, `OldAnimationsCommand`
- Ported all mixins to direct edits across `ItemRenderer`, `EntityRenderer`, `Minecraft`, `GuiScreen`, `ModelBiped`, `RenderItem`, `RenderFish`, `RenderManager`, `LayerArmorBase`, `GuiOverlayDebug`, `GuiIngame`, `GuiPlayerTabOverlay`, `ItemFood`
- Verified each port line-by-line against the original mixin sources; fixed2 self-inflicted bugs (dropped transforms from the 1.7 item matrix; `enabled` flag computed but never read so `oldBow`/`oldEating`/`oldSwordBlock` were ignored) and 2 wrong injection points (`RenderItem` had to apply at the `renderItem(stack, model)` call not method head; fishing-rod case must fall through to the 1.7 placement even when `oldRod` off)
- `./gradlew clean build` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL; jar `build/libs/GradleMCP-Base-1.8.9.jar` (~10.9 MB) contains all 8 `oldanimations` classes
- Wrote and ran a throwaway JUnit-less harness against the built jar: **all 40+ assertions pass** (defaults match upstream incl. `oldTab=false`, `/oam` alias, non-commands pass through, bad input never mutates state, case-insensitivity, whitespace tolerance). Test files deleted afterwards.

### Active
(none)

### Blocked
- **Client launch still unverified**: `java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: Can't load library: C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Roaming\.tlauncher\legacy\Minecraft\game\..\natives\windows\lwjgl64.dll` at `net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(Main.java:39)` — TLauncher natives missing, so the ported visuals have never been seen at runtime

## Next Move
1. Resolve the natives issue so the client actually launches: locate the real TLauncher natives directory and set `org.lwjgl.librarypath` in `GradleMCP.json`, or point at a vanilla1.8.9 install's `natives/`.
2. Launch via the launcher and visually verify the ported features (item position, bow pullback, sword block, eating, rod line, sneak height, red armor, punching, item-switch freeze, F3 debug screen, tab overlay, F3+B hitbox).
3. Per `README.md`, the jar may need `META-INF` deleted before dropping into `versions/GradleMCP-1.8.9/`.
4. Commit — all changes are currently uncommitted/untracked.

## Relevant Files
- `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\src\main\java\net\minecraft\oldanimations\`: new package — `OldAnimationsSettings.java` (16 toggles), `OldAnimationsCommand.java` (reflective `/oldanimations` + `/oam`), `AnimationHandler.java`, `SneakHandler.java`, `FishingLineHandler.java`, `OldAnimations.java`
- `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\src\main\java\net\minecraft\client\renderer\ItemRenderer.java`: largest port — `doBowTransformations` wrap, `isItemInUseTransformActive`, `getFirstPersonSwingProgress`, `applyOldFirstPersonTransform`, `applyFirstPersonTransformOverride`, `renderItemInFirstPerson`, `updateEquippedItem`
- `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\src\main\java\net\minecraft\client\Minecraft.java`: tick hook + `rightClickMouse` `resetBlockRemoving`
- `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\src\main\java\net\minecraft\client\renderer\EntityRenderer.java`: `getSneakAwareEyeHeight` helper, `orientCamera`, `renderWorldDirections`
- `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\src\main\java\net\minecraft\client\gui\GuiScreen.java`: chat command hook at `sendChatMessage`
- `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\src\main\java\net\minecraft\client\gui\GuiOverlayDebug.java`: 1.7 debug screen (box removal + shadow) — both left and right columns
- `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\src\main\java\net\minecraft\client\renderer\entity\RenderManager.java`: debug hitbox
- `C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\OldAnimations\OldAnimations-master\src\main\java\club\sk1er\oldanimations\`: extracted mod source, the reference for all ports — especially `AnimationHandler.java` lines 120-159 (`doFirstPersonTransform`, the exact 1.7 matrix) and `mixins/MixinItemRenderer.java`
- `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\GradleMCP.json`: launcher version manifest (`inheritsFrom: 1.8.9`, `mainClass: Start`) — needs the natives fix
- `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\build.gradle`: original deps/repos (ViaVersion removed)
- `C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\README.md`: build instructions incl. the `META-INF` deletion step

## Important Context
- Everything is **uncommitted** — `git status` shows 16 modified files plus untracked `.idea/`, `GradleMCP.json`, `run/gradle/`, `src/main/java/net/minecraft/oldanimations/`
- Build command on Windows PowerShell: `cd C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase; ./gradlew build` (use `;`, not `&&`)
- Java21 under TLauncher; vanilla 1.8.9 must be installed for `inheritsFrom` to resolve
- Pre-existing non-fatal warnings: deprecated `new Integer(...)`/`new Float(...)`/`new Short(...)`/`new Byte(...)` across many entity and optifine files
- Key original-behaviour details preserved deliberately: the 1.7 fishing rod falls through to the 1.7 placement even when `oldRod` is off; `oldTab` ships disabled; flat 2D items render with `TransformType.NONE` while 3D items keep `FIRST_PERSON` on top; the debug hitbox port skips the whole tessellator block rather than the original's `finishDrawing()`-without-`draw()` trick (same output, fewer GL calls)

param(
    [string]$GameDir   = "C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase\run",
    [string]$Java      = "C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Roaming\.tlauncher\legacy\Minecraft\jre\x64\bin\java.exe",
    [string]$McRoot    = "C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Roaming\.tlauncher\legacy\Minecraft\game",
    [string]$Version   = "GradleMCP-Base-1.8.9",
    [switch]$DryRun
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$vDir  = Join-Path $McRoot "versions\$Version"
$vJson = Join-Path $vDir "$Version.json"
$libDir = Join-Path $McRoot "libraries"
$assets = Join-Path $McRoot "assets"
$natives = Join-Path $vDir "natives"
$jar    = Join-Path $vDir "$Version.jar"

foreach ($p in @($vJson, $libDir, $assets, $natives, $jar, $Java)) {
    if (-not (Test-Path $p)) { throw "MISSING: $p" }
}

# --- Build classpath from the manifest's libraries (exact versions, no stray jars) ---
$manifest = Get-Content $vJson -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
$jars = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$jars.Add($jar)   # game jar first

foreach ($lib in $manifest.libraries) {
    $parts = $lib.name.Split(':')
    if ($parts.Count -lt 3) { continue }
    $g = $parts[0]; $a = $parts[1]; $v = $parts[2]
    $classifier = if ($parts.Count -ge 4) { $parts[3] } else { $null }

    # native-bearing artifacts are loaded via org.lwjgl.librarypath, not the classpath
    if ($a -eq 'lwjgl-platform' -or $a -eq 'jinput-platform' -or $a -eq 'twitch-external-platform') { continue }

    $file = if ($classifier) { "$a-$v-$classifier.jar" } else { "$a-$v.jar" }
    $path = Join-Path $libDir (Join-Path ($g.Replace('.', '\')) "$a\$v\$file")
    if (Test-Path $path) { $jars.Add($path) }
    else { Write-Host "  [skip] not downloaded: $($lib.name)" }
}

$cp = ($jars -join ';')
Write-Host "classpath entries: $($jars.Count)"

# --- JVM args ---
# Java 17+ needs opens for Guava 17 / LWJGL2 / 1.8.9 itself; natives go on librarypath.
$opens = @(
    'java.base/java.lang', 'java.base/java.lang.reflect', 'java.base/java.util',
    'java.base/java.io',   'java.base/java.net',           'java.base/java.nio',
    'java.base/java.text', 'java.base/java.util.concurrent',
    'java.base/sun.nio.ch','java.base/jdk.internal.misc',
    'java.desktop/java.awt','java.desktop/java.awt.event',
    'java.desktop/sun.awt','java.desktop/sun.java2d',
    'java.management/sun.management'
) | ForEach-Object { "--add-opens=$($_)=ALL-UNNAMED" }

$jvmArgs = @(
    "-Xmx2G"
    "-Djava.library.path=$natives"
    "-Dorg.lwjgl.librarypath=$natives"
    "-Dnet.java.games.input.librarypath=$natives"
    "-Dorg.lwjgl.util.Debug=false"
    "-Dfile.encoding=UTF-8"
) + $opens

$uuid = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'
$mcArgs = @(
    '--tweakClass','net.minecraft.launchwrapper.Launch'
    '--username','Dev'
    '--version',$Version
    '--gameDir',$GameDir
    '--assetsDir',$assets
    '--assetIndex','1.8'
    '--uuid',$uuid
    '--accessToken','0'
    '--userProperties','{}'
    '--userType','legacy'
    '--versionType','release'
)

$argv = @()
$argv += $jvmArgs
$argv += '-cp', $cp
$argv += 'net.minecraft.launchwrapper.Launch'
$argv += $mcArgs

Write-Host "mainClass: $($manifest.mainClass)   natives: $natives   gameDir: $GameDir"
if ($DryRun) { Write-Host "`n--- ARGV ---"; $argv | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  $_" }; exit 0 }

& $Java @argv
exit $LASTEXITCODE

# GradleMCPBase
Gradle MCP for 1.8.9 with optifine

# How to setup
Clone the repository into whatever folder you want (Mine is in my coding folder), open the project in Intellij IDEA then make a new run configuration (Application)
and copy everything from the image below.

Now you can start Minecraft!

![run_config](https://github.com/AbyssClient/GradleMCPBase/assets/170053471/c52c81f5-d339-434b-9220-290cf5a5e019)

# How to build
Just run the "build" run command in the gradle tab

Once you've done that go into the build/libs directory inside of the GradleMCP-Base folder

Three distinct issues, each masking the next:

1. **launchwrapper 1.11 can't load on Java 9+** — `ClassCastException: AppClassLoader cannot be cast to URLClassLoader` at `Launch.java:34`. 3. **`sourceCompatibility` alone wasn't enough.** It only sets the bytecode version; javac still *linked* against JDK 17's API. OptiFine's `Shaders.<clinit>` resolved `ByteBuffer.limit(int)` to the Java 9+ covariant `ByteBuffer` return type, which doesn't exist on Java 8 → `NoSuchMethodError` during crash reporting, which then **hid the real crash**. `options.release = 8` pins the API surface. The hook sits **before** `thePlayer.sendChatMessage(msg)`, so matched commands never reach the server. That matters: `/fov` handled server-side would only work in single-player and would be rejected or rate-limited on most servers. Client-side means it works everywhere.

```java
if (ClientCommands.handle(this.mc, msg))
{
    return;
}

this.mc.thePlayer.sendChatMessage(msg);
```

Verified in the deployed bytecode:

```
GuiScreen  -> invokestatic ClientCommands.handle:(Lnet/minecraft/client/Minecraft;Ljava/lang/String;)Z
FovCommand -> invokevirtual GameSettings.setOptionFloatValue:(Lnet/minecraft/client/settings/GameSettings$Options;F)V
```

## Three decisions worth flagging

**It uses `setOptionFloatValue`, not the `fovSetting` field.** That field is stored in **degrees**, but `options.txt` persists it normalized as `(fov - 70) / 40`. Going through the setter keeps that encoding consistent so the value survives a restart.

**`NaN` and `Infinity` are rejected explicitly.** `Float.parseFloat("NaN")` succeeds, and clamping propagates `NaN` through `Math.min`/`Math.max` — that would poison the projection matrix and black-screen the client. Worth having, since `/fov` is exactly the kind of command someone pastes a weird value into.

**I kept vanilla's `addToSentMessages` before the consume**, so `/fov 90` still shows in your up-arrow history like any other typed message.

Two things I did not do: register a `/help` entry (client commands aren't visible to the server's command list, so there's no obvious place to surface it), and add an alias like `/fov` → `/fov reset`. Say the word if you want either.

Untested at runtime — that's the part I can't do for you.

## What changed

Vanilla 1.8.9 calls `setupViewBobbing` from **three** places, and it was driving both the camera and the hand off one `viewBobbing` flag:

| Call site | What it moves | Now gated on |
|---|---|---|
| `EntityRenderer:838` | the **world/camera** — drags the crosshair | `viewBobbing && cameraBobbing` |

| `EntityRenderer:968` | the **hand/item** overlay pass | `viewBobbing` |

One-line behavioural change plus a new `GameSettings.cameraBobbing`, defaulting to **false**:

```java
// The camera bob moves the whole world, which drags the crosshair around while aiming.
// The hand still bobs via renderHand, so gate only this one on the extra setting.
if (this.mc.gameSettings.viewBobbing && this.mc.gameSettings.cameraBobbing)
{
    this.setupViewBobbing(partialTicks);
}
```

I reused vanilla's `setupViewBobbing` untouched rather than rewriting the trigonometry — the hand bob is exactly the vanilla motion, just no longer doubled up by a camera bob.

## Persistence

New `bobCamera` key in `options.txt`, wired into load, save, and `resetSettings` (default `false`), alongside the existing `bobView`.

## `/bob` command

```
/bob           → "Hand bobbing is on, camera bobbing is off."
/bob hand      → hand bobs, camera steady     (default, minimal)
/bob camera    → full vanilla bobbing
/bob off       → nothing bobs
```

## Two things to know

**Vanilla's "View Bobbing" option still controls the hand.** Turning it off in Video Settings kills hand bobbing; it no longer has any effect on the camera. Your launcher's `options.txt` currently has `bobView:false`, so **hand bobbing will be off until you flip that on** — via the Video Settings menu or `/bob hand`.

Vanilla 1.8.9 has no always-sprint; you double-tap W or hold the sprint key. I added a block in `EntityPlayerSP.onLivingUpdate()` that runs **after** vanilla's own sprint logic, so it wins over the stop condition:

```java
// Runs after the vanilla sprint checks above so it wins over the stop condition.
// The same guards vanilla uses are kept, otherwise this would sprint while
// sneaking, eating, blind, or on an empty hunger bar.
if (this.mc.gameSettings.alwaysSprint && !this.isSprinting() && !this.isSneaking()
    && this.movementInput.moveForward >= f && !this.isCollidedHorizontally
    && flag3 && !this.isUsingItem() && !this.isPotionActive(Potion.blindness))
{

}
```

messages.summary:
## Objective
Port Sk1er's "Old Animations" mod into the MCP 1.8.9 base, then (per later user request) remove it entirely and add new client-side features: `/fov` chat command and hand-only view bobbing.

## Requirements
- Original port: convert Forge/Mixin/Essential code into plain MCP source; do NOT add those frameworks
- Remove all Old Animations mod code once the port proved unverifiable visually
- `/fov <fov>` in-game command to change FOV
- "minimal view bobbing" = bob the hand only, do NOT bob the camera/aim
- **Standing rule: never launch the client after a build** (user instruction, applies going forward)
- Verify with `./gradlew build`; commit only when asked (not yet asked)

## Decisions
- Every mixin became a direct source edit; `MixinOnlineIndicator` dropped entirely (Essential-only)
- Client-side commands consumed in `GuiScreen.sendChatMessage(String, boolean)` *before* `thePlayer.sendChatMessage` — server-side would fail on multiplayer and be rate-limited
- `/fov` uses `GameSettings.setOptionFloatValue(FOV, v)`, not the `fovSetting` field, because `fovSetting` is stored in degrees but persisted to options.txt normalized as `(fov-70)/40`
- `/fov` explicitly rejects `NaN`/`Infinity` — `Float.parseFloat` accepts them and clamping propagates NaN into the projection matrix (black screen)
- Bobbing: reused vanilla `setupViewBobbing` untouched; added `cameraBobbing` (default false) gating only the world/camera call site. Vanilla `viewBobbing` still controls the hand
- Kept three non-mod changes: `EntityLivingBase` jump cooldown (separate user request), `Cartesian.java` cast fix (required to compile on JDK 17), `build.gradle` `options.release = 8`
- `Start.java` rewritten to supply option defaults only when the caller didn't pass them, since the manifest's `minecraftArguments` already supplies them

## Work State
### Completed
- Full read of all 12 mixins, 3 handlers, config, command, resources from extracted mod
- Ported all mixins across 12 vanilla files; verified line-by-line against originals- Removed the entire port: reverted 14 files, verified 0 `oldanimations|OldAnimations|oldBow|oldEating|oldSwordBlock|oldRod` matches in `src`, 0 entries in jar
- Fixed two launch blockers that were masking each other (see Important Context)
- Added `/fov` command (3 files in `net.minecraft.client.commands`) + `GuiScreen` hook
- Added hand-only view bobbing: `cameraBobbing` setting + `/bob` command + `EntityRenderer:838` gate
- Verified all changes at bytecode level in the deployed jar via `javap -c`
- Multiple clean builds green (latest: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 2m 35s`, 0 errors), deployed to launcher version dir with `META-INF` stripped each time

### Active
(none)

### Blocked
- **No visual verification possible**: this model has no image input, so screenshots and the user's attached PNG both come back unreadable. Runtime confirmation of bobbing intensity and `/fov` effect is on the user.
- (resolved) natives/launchwrapper/Java-version issues — all fixed

### Next Move

## Commands

```
/fps                     → toggle readout on/off
/fps mode smooth         → interpolated, updates every frame, one decimal
/fps mode normal         → vanilla behaviour, whole number, sampled once per second
/fps size <0.5-8>        → text scale factor, 1.0 = normal GUI font
/fps pos <x> <y> [alpha] → move it; negative x/y anchor to right/bottom edge
```

Defaults: off, `normal`, size `1.0`, pos `4, 4`, alpha `255`.

## How the two modes actually differ

They're genuinely different sources, not a relabelling. `normal` reads `Minecraft.getDebugFPS()`, which is only assigned once per second inside a `while` loop in `runTick` — so it steps, and can sit stale for up to a second.

`smooth` needed per-frame data, so I added a `getFpsCounter()` getter to `Minecraft` (the field was package-private and already incremented once per frame) and run an exponential moving average over the frame deltas. It reports `%.1f`, starts at `-- FPS` for the first frame, and resets on every toggle or mode change so it never eases in from a stale value.

Colour is green ≥55, yellow ≥25, red below.

If you meant something else by `z` (draw layer, a vertical offset in unscaled space), say which and it's a small change.

**Not persisted.** FPS display config lives in static fields on `FpsOverlay`, not in `GameSettings`, so it resets on restart. `/fov` and `/bob` *are* persisted to `options.txt`. Done. Built, tested headlessly, deployed. Not launched.

## `fpsdisplay.cfg`

Lives next to `options.txt` in the game dir (`.../game/fpsdisplay.cfg`):

```
# FPS display configuration - written by /fps
enabled=false
mode=normal
size=1.0
posX=4
posY=4
alpha=255
```

`key=value`, `#` comments, blank lines skipped. Unknown keys are ignored, so a config written by a later build stays loadable by this one.

## Load / save / reset

- **load** — `FpsOverlay.load()`, called from `Minecraft.startGame()` right after `GameSettings` is constructed. Verified in bytecode at offset 16, immediately following the `gameSettings` store.
- **save** — called by *every* mutator (`setEnabled`, `setMode`, `setSize`, `setPos`, `reset`). Deliberately not an exit hook: vanilla 1.8.9 never saves `options.txt` on quit either, and writing on change means a crash can't lose the config.
- **reset** — `/fps reset`, restores all six defaults and rewrites the file.

## Two decisions worth flagging

**Validated on read, not trusted.** A hand-edited `mode=teleport`, `size=abc` or `alpha=99999` logs a warning and falls back per-key rather than corrupting the overlay. Valid keys in the same file still apply — a broken line doesn't poison its neighbours.

**Clamping moved into the setters.** Previously `FpsCommand` clamped size and alpha before calling. That meant the config file could hold values the overlay never validated. Now `setSize`/`setPos` clamp, so the bounds hold no matter the caller.

## Verification

I couldn't launch, but `getConfigFile()` falls back to `new File(".")` when `Minecraft.getMinecraft()` is null — so I drove the real compiled class from a scratch directory under the full runtime classpath. 38 checks, all passing:

- default file contents, and reset idempotency across two calls
- round-trip of all six values (set → wipe memory → load from disk)
- clamping at 999, 0.01, `NaN`, `Infinity`, alpha 99999 and -40
- hostile file mixing valid and malformed keys
- binary garbage, missing file, and that `load` does **not** recreate a deleted file

My first harness run showed 9 failures. Those were test bugs, not code bugs — `reset()` saves defaults over the file, so the round-trip fixture wiped itself, and leftover sentinel values made the "defaults" assertions fail. Fixed by adding a `clearMemory()` that resets fields without saving.

One thing still unverified: `load()` running inside `startGame()` at actual startup, since that path needs a live `Minecraft`. The bytecode confirms the call site; the disk behaviour it reads is what I tested.

Two real bugs found in my code:

1. **"explicit autoColour honoured" FAIL**: file has `autoColour=true` then `colour=#123456`. My `applySetting` processes keys in file order. `autoColour=true` sets autoColour=true, then `colour=#123456` sets `autoColour=false`. So the last one wins, ignoring the explicit `autoColour=true`.

This is a genuine order-dependence bug. The `save()` always writes `autoColour` BEFORE `colour`, so a saved file with autoColour=true and a leftover stored colour (e.g. after `/fps color #123456` then `/fps color auto`) would write:

```
colour=#123456
```

Fix: make `colour` parsing NOT touch autoColour. Instead, have the autoColour key be authoritative. But then how does `setColour` persist "auto off"? Need a separate flag.

- `autoColour=true|false`

I implemented `color` (your message said "corlor" — `colour` works too as an alias).

## Commands

```
/fps color #FF8800      → pin to a fixed colour
/fps color auto         → back to green/yellow/red by frame rate
/fps shadow on|off      → toggle the drop shadow
```

Hex accepts `#RRGGBB` or bare `ff8800`, any case. Strictly 6 digits — `#FFF`, `#FF8800FF` and named colours are rejected with a hint. `/fps color` and `/fps shadow` with no argument report the current value.

Setting a fixed colour turns the frame-rate colour coding **off**, which is why `auto` exists as the way back.

## Two bugs the harness caught

Both were mine, both real, both reachable:

**1. The config couldn't round-trip its own output.** `save()` writes `autoColour` before `colour`. So `/fps color #123456` then `/fps color auto` writes:

```
autoColour=true
colour=#123456
```

On reload the `colour` line overwrote `autoColour`, re-pinning you to the colour you'd just unset. Fixed by recording which keys the file actually contained and resolving them after the parse, so `autoColour` wins regardless of line order — while a hand-written file with only `colour=` still correctly implies auto off.

**2. A typo silently turned shadow off.** `value.equalsIgnoreCase("true")` means `shadow=yes` parses as `false`. Harmless for `enabled` (default is already false, which hid it), not harmless for `shadow`. Replaced with a strict `parseBooleanOr` that keeps the current value and logs.

## Also fixed while in there

The render path was calling `drawStringWithShadow` *and* `drawString` — the text was being drawn twice every frame whenever `size != 1.0`. It's now a genuine either/or: one call, shadow on or off.

## Config now

```
enabled=false
mode=normal
size=1.0
posX=4
posY=4
alpha=255
autoColour=true
colour=#FFFFFF
shadow=true
```

`shadow` defaults to **on** — previously it was implicitly off at size 1.0, which was inconsistent.

## Verification

Harness is up to 76 checks, all passing against the compiled class: 14 hex-parsing cases (including rejection of `red`, `0xFF0000`, 3/5/8-digit), colour and shadow round-trips, the order-independence case, bad booleans, `0xFFFFFFFF` masked to `RRGGBB`, plus the existing file round-trip and corruption suites.

NoHurtCam added. Built, deployed, not launched.

```
/nhk        → toggle
/nhk on     → no tilt on damage
/nhk off    → vanilla
```

`noHurtCam` defaults to **false**, persisted in `options.txt` as `noHurtCam:` — load, save and `resetSettings` all wired, matching `cameraBobbing`.

## The change

One gate, inside `EntityRenderer.hurtCameraEffect`:

```java
// NoHurtCam skips only the damage tilt. The death roll above is left alone:
// removing that too would leave no feedback at all that you died.
if (this.mc.gameSettings.noHurtCam || f < 0.0F)
{
    return;
}
```

Two things I decided deliberately:

**Gated in the method, not at the call sites.** `hurtCameraEffect` has three callers — `setupCameraTransform` plus both hand passes at 926 and 965. Vanilla applies the hurt shake to the camera *and* to the item in hand. Gating at the call sites would have meant three edits that could drift apart; gating inside covers all three by construction. Bytecode confirms three call sites, one gate.

**Kept the death roll.** `hurtCameraEffect` does two unrelated things: the damage tilt, and a 40°-to-8000° roll while health is 0. I only gated the tilt. Removing both is a defensible reading of "no hurt cam", but you'd get no visual feedback at all that you'd died, which felt like the wrong trade. Easy to change if you want it gone.

Also untouched: the red damage flash. That's `hurtTime` driving a GUI overlay in `EntityLivingBase`, a separate effect.

## Verified

- `getfield GameSettings.noHurtCam` at offset 77, `ifne` jumping past the tilt — and the death roll's `GlStateManager.rotate` at 67 sits *before* it, confirming death cam survives
- three `putfield noHurtCam` in `GameSettings` (load / save / reset)
- `NhkCommand` constructed in `ClientCommands`

The FPS config harness is untouched by this and still passes; I didn't re-run it since nothing in `FpsOverlay` changed.

Untested at runtime, as always. The thing to judge by eye is the hand: since the tilt is gated centrally, the item in hand stops shaking too, which is the expected behaviour but not something you can confirm from bytecode.

## Objective
Add client-side quality-of-life commands/features to the MCP 1.8.9 base (Forge's MCP "GradleMCP-Base"): `/fov`, hand-only view bobbing, always-sprint, an FPS overlay with a `.cfg` file, and NoHurtCam — each built, verified, and deployed to a TLauncher version directory.

## Requirements
- Convert features into plain MCP source; do NOT add Forge/Mixin/Essential frameworks
- **Standing rule: never launch the client after a build** (user instruction, applies going forward)
- Verify with `./gradlew build`; commit only when asked (never asked)
- `/fps` subcommands: `mode smooth|normal`, `size <size>`, `pos <x y z>` (three values)
- `/fps corlor <hex>` (user's typo for color) and `/fps shadow <on/off>`
- `/nhk <on/off>` for nohurtcam
- Persistence via load/save/reset plus a `.cfg` file

## Decisions
- Client commands consumed in `GuiScreen.sendChatMessage(String, boolean)` *before* `thePlayer.sendChatMessage` — server-side would fail on multiplayer and be rate-limited
- `/fov` uses `GameSettings.setOptionFloatValue(FOV, v)`, not the `fovSetting` field (`fovSetting` is degrees but persisted as `(fov-70)/40`); explicitly rejects `NaN`/`Infinity` because clamping propagates NaN into the projection matrix (black screen)
- Bobbing: reused vanilla `setupViewBobbing` untouched; `cameraBobbing` (default false) gates only the world/camera call site; vanilla `viewBobbing` still controls the hand
- FPS `normal` = `Minecraft.getDebugFPS()` (assigned once per second, steps); `smooth` = EMA over per-frame deltas using a new `Minecraft.getFpsCounter()` getter, reports `%.1f`, starts `-- FPS`, resets on toggle/mode change
- FPS `pos` z-axis mapped to **alpha (0–255)**, optional, validated not clamped; negative x/y anchor to right/bottom edge. Flagged to user as a guess
- FPS shadow defaults to **on**; previously implicitly off at size 1.0
- FPS config in static fields on `FpsOverlay` + separate `fpsdisplay.cfg` (not `GameSettings`); saved on *every* mutator rather than an exit hook, because vanilla 1.8.9 never saves `options.txt` on quit either
- Config values validated on read, not trusted; per-key fallback on bad values; unknown keys ignored for forward compat
- NoHurtCam gated **inside** `EntityRenderer.hurtCameraEffect` (one edit covers all 3 call sites: camera + both hand passes) rather than at call sites
- NoHurtCam keeps the death roll and red damage flash; only the damage tilt is gated
- `/nhk`, `/bob`, `/sprint` toggle when given no args; added `Minecraft.getFpsCounter()` getter
- Kept three non-mod changes: `EntityLivingBase` jump cooldown (separate user request), `Cartesian.java` cast fix (required to compile on JDK 17), `build.gradle` `options.release = 8`

## Work State
### Completed
- Old Animations port fully removed (14 files reverted, 0 matches in `src`, 0 entries in jar)
- Fixed two masking launch bugs (natives path; duplicate `--version`/`--accessToken` from manifest)
- `/fov`, `/bob`, always-sprint, `/fps` overlay + `fpsdisplay.cfg` (load/save/reset), `/fps color`, `/fps shadow`, `/nhk`
- Fixed real bugs found by headless harness: config order-dependence (`autoColour`/`colour` resolution via `Presence` class), lenient boolean parse (`shadow=yes` silently off → strict `parseBooleanOr`), double text draw in render path
- Multiple clean builds green (latest: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 40s`, 0 errors); deployed each time with `META-INF` stripped
- Bytecode verification of every hook via `javap -c -p` in the deployed jar

### Active
(none)

### Blocked
- **No visual verification possible**: model has no image input; screenshots and user-attached PNGs come back unreadable. Runtime confirmation of bobbing intensity, `/fov` effect, `/fps` easing/appearance, and NoHurtCam hand behaviour is on the user.

### Next Move
1. Await user direction; nothing pending. Likely candidates: commit the work (never committed), or add more commands.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/commands/`: new package — `ClientCommand.java` (interface), `ClientCommands.java` (dispatcher; `handle()` returns true if consumed), `FovCommand.java`, `BobCommand.java`, `SprintCommand.java`, `NhkCommand.java`, `FpsCommand.java`, `FpsOverlay.java` (rendering + config; nested `Mode`, `Presence`)
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/gui/GuiScreen.java`: one-line hook at `sendChatMessage(String, boolean)` + `import net.minecraft.client.commands.ClientCommands`
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/gui/GuiIngame.java`: `FpsOverlay.render(...)` call right after the `showDebugInfo` block
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/renderer/EntityRenderer.java`: `hurtCameraEffect` noHurtCam gate (~606-631); `setupViewBobbing` 633; bob gate 838; hand calls 926/965/968
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/settings/GameSettings.java`: `cameraBobbing`/`alwaysSprint`/`noHurtCam` fields, load/save/`resetSettings`
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/Minecraft.java`: `getFpsCounter()` getter; `FpsOverlay.load()` at start of `startGame()` (offset 16, after `gameSettings` store)
- `build.gradle`: `java { sourceCompatibility/targetCompatibility = 1.8 }` + `tasks.withType(JavaCompile) { options.release = 8 }`
- `src/main/java/Start.java`: rewritten with `addDefault`/`hasOption`; still sets `org.lwjgl.librarypath` to `../natives/<os>`
- `C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\FpsCfgTest.java`: 76-check headless harness for FpsOverlay config (uses `clearMemory()` via reflection; `declared()` for package-private `parseHexOr`)
- `C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\cp.txt`: full runtime classpath (145 gradle-cache jars) for the harness
- `C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Roaming\.tlauncher\legacy\Minecraft\game\versions\GradleMCP-Base-1.8.9\`: deployed jar + json + natives
- `C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Roaming\.tlauncher\legacy\Minecraft\natives\windows\`: 14 DLLs created to fix natives path (outside project; delete to undo)
- `C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\port-backup\`: patch + 14 reverted files + compiled jar (Old Animations restore point)

## Important Context
- **Build command on PowerShell**: `cd C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase; ./gradlew build` (use `;`, not `&&`). Pre-existing non-fatal deprecation warnings for `new Integer/Float/Short/Byte(...)`.
- **Verification technique**: `FpsOverlay.getConfigFile()` falls back to `new File(".")` when `Minecraft.getMinecraft()` is null, so config load/save/reset is testable headlessly by running the compiled class from a scratch dir. Build the classpath by globbing non-source/non-natives jars from the gradle cache.
- **Two harness bugs were in my own test, not the code**: `reset()` saves defaults over the file (so it can't seed a round-trip fixture — use `clearMemory()`), and leftover sentinel values break "defaults" assertions.
- Deployed jar is intentionally **not** byte-identical to `build/libs` output: `META-INF/` and `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` are stripped. Verified the only entries missing are those two.
- `options.release = 8` is required, not just `sourceCompatibility`: Gradle's JDK 17 links `ByteBuffer.limit(int)` to the Java 9+ covariant return type → `NoSuchMethodError` in OptiFine's `Shaders.<clinit>`, which then *hid* the real crash inside `CrashReport.getCompleteReport()`.
- Client ran ~8 min successfully on Java 8u51 previously (PID 15080): natives loaded, LWJGL 2.9.4, world `mcpworld` loaded/saved, clean shutdown. Exit code 1 from the PowerShell wrapper is not a failure.
- `org.lwjgl.librarypath` resolution: TLauncher CWD is `game\`, so `../natives/windows` resolves to `Minecraft\natives\windows\`. Running from IDEA requires working directory `run\`.
- Launcher `game/options.txt` has `bobView:false` → hand bobbing OFF on first run. Use `/bob hand` or the Video Settings menu.
- `fpsdisplay.cfg` won't exist until you run `/fps` or change something — `load()` doesn't create a missing file (verified intentional).
- TLauncher regenerates the version manifest, so manual edits to `versions/.../GradleMCP-Base-1.8.9.json` get clobbered.
- `_JAVA_OPTIONS` is set in the environment and injects JVM options from outside the launcher.
- Everything remains **uncommitted**.

Both mods are ported as commands, built, verified, and deployed. I did **not** launch the client.

## What I found

Both classes you pointed at were settings-only — the behaviour lived in 7 mixins elsewhere in that project. I read the mixins and the shader resources to port the actual behaviour.

## `/anim` — Old Animations

`Animations.java` holds all 10 settings plus a master switch (off by default, so vanilla is untouched until `/anim on`). Hooks:

| Setting | Hook |
|---|---|
| `blockhit` | 4× `transformFirstPersonItem` in `renderItemInFirstPerson`; third-person arm pose in `LayerHeldItem`; fakes the swing + crack particles in `sendClickBlockToController` |
| `pushing` | `PlayerControllerMP.getIsHittingBlock()` returns false so the server is never asked to break a block |
| `pushingparticles` | gates `addBlockHitEffects` |
| `sneak` | `EntityRenderer.orientCamera` + `renderWorldDirections` eye height; crouch offset moved ahead of `postRenderArm` in `LayerHeldItem` |
| `smoothsneak` / `smoothspeed` | frame-rate-independent easing, ported from `SimpleAnimation` + `AnimationUtils.calculateCompensation` |
| `health` | suppresses the two damage-overlay heart draws in `renderPlayerStats` |
| `armordamage` | `LayerArmorBase.shouldCombineTextures` |
| `switch` | replaces `updateEquippedItem` |
| `rod` | old fishing-rod pose for flat items |

## `/mb` — Motion Blur

`MotionBlur.java` with both backends: `shader` (blends previous frame; added `shaders/post/motion_blur.json` + `.fsh` + `.vsh`, and a `getListShaders()` accessor on `ShaderGroup` to reach the `BlurFactor` uniform) and `accum` (`glAccum` in `updateDisplay`, self-disables on `GL_INVALID_OPERATION` like the original).

Config in `animations.cfg` / `motionblur.cfg`, saved on every change.

## Three deliberate deviations from the source

1. **Item switch polarity was inverted.** The source used `flag ? 1.0F : 0.0F` where vanilla uses `flag ? 0.0F : 1.0F`. That drives `equippedProgress` to 1 (lowered) precisely when you *aren't* swapping — it would have parked your held item off-screen. I used vanilla's polarity.
2. **`smoothSneak` is gated on the master switch.** The source applied it even when the mod was off, which would make `/anim off` not mean "off".
3. **Dropped two unused GLSL declarations** (`oneTexel`, `InSize`) from `motion_blur.fsh` — they were declared in the fragment stage but never written by any vertex shader, which is a link error on strict drivers.

## Verification

- Build green; **96-check headless harness passes** (defaults, master gating, round-trip, bad/unknown values, clamping, NaN/Infinity, reset, shader JSON structure).
- The harness caught a **real bug I'd written**: `applySetting` used a hardcoded `false` fallback, so a typo'd `blockHit=yes` silently switched a default-*on* setting off. Now falls back to the stored value.
- All 24 hook call sites confirmed in the right methods via `javap` on the deployed jar; config loads confirmed in `startGame()`.
- Deployed jar differs from `build/libs` only by `META-INF/` and `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF`.

Two caveats I can't test for you: **`/mb accum`** will most likely switch itself off on your driver (no accumulation buffer), and shader mode needs `OpenGlHelper.shadersSupported`. Worth confirming `/mb`, `/anim sneak`, and `/anim blockhit` visually — and everything is still uncommitted.

```java
GlStateManager.matrixMode(5889);
GlStateManager.pushMatrix();
GlStateManager.loadIdentity();
... projectionMatrix ...
GlStateManager.popMatrix();
```

content.text:
The user wants:
1. A `/freelook` command with `mode <hold/toggle>`
2. A bind option in Options > Controls (keybind)

Free look = third-person camera that follows only mouse movement, not player body rotation. Classic free look.

Let me think about implementation for MCP 1.8.9:

Free look implementation typically:
- When active, the camera orbits around the player without rotating the player's body
- `EntityRenderer.renderViewEntity` is set to a dummy/wrapper entity whose yaw/pitch are decoupled from the player
- The classic approach: create an `Entity` wrapper whose `rotationYaw`/`rotationPitch` are set from mouse deltas, and set it as the render view entity, so the world renders from it but the player body doesn't turn.

Common implementations:
1. Set `mc.objectMouseOver`... no.
2. Use `Minecraft.getRenderViewEntity()` — set to a custom entity.
3. Simpler approach used by many mods: in `EntityRenderer.setupCameraTransform` / `orientCamera`, override `thirdPersonDistanceTemp` and rotate the camera by freelook yaw/pitch deltas, and counter-rotate so the player model stays put.

Actually the most common and robust approach for MC 1.8.9 free look:

In `Minecraft.runTick()` / mouse handling: when free look is active, instead of applying mouse deltas to `thePlayer.rotationYaw/rotationPitch`, apply them to separate `freelookYaw`/`freelookPitch`. Then in `EntityRenderer.orientCamera` (or `setupCameraTransform`), add those offsets to the camera rotation.

But the cleanest way that keeps the player model facing forward: set the render view entity to a wrapper entity.

Let me think about what's practical and safe here.

Approach A: Camera-rotation offset (simplest)
- Track `freelookYaw`, `freelookPitch` (floats)
- In `Minecraft.runTick()` where mouse input is processed: if freelook active, add deltas to freelook vars instead of player rotation; else normal
- In `EntityRenderer.orientCamera`, after computing camera rotation, apply the freelook offsets via `GlStateManager.rotate`

Problem: `orientCamera` sets `this.cloudFog`... it computes a quaternion `q` from yaw/pitch/roll and calls `GlStateManager.rotate(q)`. Applying extra rotation after that would rotate the camera but the player model is rendered separately in `renderWorld` → `RenderGlobal.renderEntities` which uses `RenderManager.renderEntity` with its own rotations. Actually the player model is rendered in world space, not view space, so rotating the camera does keep the player body facing its original direction. 

So Approach A works: rotate the camera by the freelook offset, player model stays put. That IS free look.

But there's a catch: mouse sensitivity/pitch clamping. And when freelook is off, the offsets must reset to 0.

Also `Entity.rayTrace` / `objectMouseOver` — the block the player is looking at is computed from `thePlayer` rotation in `EntityRenderer.getMouseOver()` (or `Minecraft`). In 1.8.9, `EntityRenderer.getMouseOver()` uses `mc.objectMouseOver = entity.rayTrace(...)` based on the player's rotation. With free look active, the crosshair should correspond to where the camera looks. Hmm, in vanilla, rayTrace uses `this.rotationYaw/rotationPitch` of the player.

For a good free look, the raytrace should use the camera direction. Many implementations leave it as-is (slight inconsistency) or handle it.

Let me look at how 1.8.9 computes objectMouseOver to decide.

Actually, a cleaner and very common approach for MC free look mods:

Approach B: Wrapper render view entity
Create a dummy `Entity` (e.g., `Entity` subclass or reuse `EntityOtherClientPlayer`) that copies the player's position but has independent rotation. Set `mc.setRenderViewEntity(wrapper)`. Then all camera code (orientCamera, rayTrace via `getMouseOver` using renderViewEntity?) works naturally.

In 1.8.9, `EntityRenderer.getMouseOver()`:
```java
public void getMouseOver(float partialTicks) {
    ...
    Entity entity = this.mc.getRenderViewEntity();
    if (entity != null) {
        ...
        this.mc.objectMouseOver = entity.rayTrace(d0, partialTicks);
```
Yes! It uses `this.mc.getRenderViewEntity()`. So with a wrapper, the raytrace follows the camera. 

And `EntityPlayer.getEyeHeight()` — the wrapper would need proper eye height. If I use `EntityOtherClientPlayer` it has player eye height. Or I can subclass.

Hmm, but there's risk: `getRenderViewEntity()` is used for lots of things — particle culling, fog, boss bars, `GuiIngame.renderPlayerStats` (needs EntityPlayer for hearts!), spectator, etc. If I set it to a non-player entity, the HUD breaks (no hearts, no food).

Done and deployed. Here's what landed.

## `/freelook` + Controls binding

**`/freelook`** — bare shows status, `mode <hold|toggle>` sets the mode, `on|off` the master switch, `reset` restores defaults. Settings persist to `freelook.cfg`.

**Keybind** — real vanilla `KeyBinding` (`keyBindFreeLook`), so it appears under Options → Controls → Miscellaneous and persists in `options.txt` like any other key. Defaults to **V**, which vanilla leaves unbound. `/freelook` reports the current key and tells you to bind one if it's unbound.

### How it works

The key insight from reading vanilla: **every mouse-look update funnels through one call**, `thePlayer.setAngles(f2, f3)` in `EntityRenderer.updateCameraAndRender`. That's the only place raw deltas become rotation. So `EntityPlayerSP.setAngles` is intercepted — while free look is active the deltas accumulate into private yaw/pitch offsets and the body never turns. Three hooks total:

1. `EntityPlayerSP.setAngles` — divert the deltas
2. `EntityRenderer.orientCamera` — add the offsets to the view
3. `EntityPlayerSP.getLook` — add them to the look vector, so the **crosshair, block outline and block breaking follow the camera**, not the body

I deliberately never mutate `rotationYaw`/`rotationPitch`. That keeps walking direction, the rendered player model, and the packets sent to the server all consistent — which is what makes it *behave* rather than just look different. Verified: the player model renderer reads those fields directly, so body and head stay put.

### A bug I caught in my own first attempt

I initially folded the offsets into `f1`/`f2` in the third-person branch. Working through the matrix, that pair acts on the camera-offset vector and **must be identity** for the camera to land at `eye − viewDir·d3`. With free look folded in, the camera would have sat at body pitch **plus twice** the free-look pitch. Fixed by keeping `f1`/`f2` on the body angles and giving the collision raytrace its own `rayYaw`/`rayPitch` — so wall clipping still follows the camera. That reasoning is in a comment at the site so it doesn't get "simplified" back later.

- `clean build` → `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, 0 errors
- **47 headless checks** on the state machine: hold/toggle edge detection, master-switch gating, pitch clamp at ±90° under5000 frames, yaw wrap, decay convergence, frame-rate independence (one 60 ms step ≈ four 15 ms steps), config round-trip and malformed-input handling
- **8 checks** that the bind is actually in the `keyBindings` array with no collision against any vanilla default
- All hooks confirmed in bytecode via `javap`, in the correct methods
- Deployed jar: 7161 entries, **zero** `MotionBlur`/`motion_blur` entries, `FreeLook*` present, `key.freeLook` in the lang file

## Objective
Port Glide client mods into the MCP 1.8.9 base (GradleMCPBase) as command-driven settings, build, verify, and deploy to a TLauncher version directory. Motion blur was removed on request; free look with `/freelook mode <hold|toggle>` and an Options→Controls keybind was added.

## Requirements
- Convert features into plain MCP source; do NOT add Forge/Mixin/Essential frameworks
- **Standing rule: never launch the client after a build**
- **Standing rule: do NOT build the Glide client**
- Verify with `./gradlew build`; commit only when asked (never asked)
- Persistence via load/save/reset plus `.cfg` files
- Do not leave stray files in the Glide repo (used CLI flag instead of adding `gradle.properties`)

## Decisions
- `/anim`, `/mb`, `/freelook` consumed in `GuiScreen.sendChatMessage(String, boolean)` via `ClientCommands.handle()`
- Animations: 10 settings + master switch, all off by default (`/anim on` opts in); config `animations.cfg`
- **Motion blur fully removed** at user request ("motionblur is so broken, remove it plese"): deleted `MotionBlur.java`, `MotionBlurCommand.java`, 3 shader files, all hooks/imports, plus `ShaderGroup.getListShaders()` (added only for motion blur, so it was dead code)
- Free look intercepts `EntityPlayerSP.setAngles` — the single place vanilla converts mouse deltas to rotation. Body rotation is **never mutated**, so walking direction, player model, and server packets stay consistent
- Only 3 hooks: `EntityPlayerSP.setAngles` (divert deltas), `EntityRenderer.orientCamera` (add offsets to view), `EntityPlayerSP.getLook` (add offsets so crosshair/outline/block-breaking follow the camera)
- Free look starts **enabled** (unlike other features) since it is inert until a key is bound; default bind **V (47)**, vanilla-unbound
- `FreeLook.step(float,float,boolean)` is package-private so the state machine is testable without a running game
- Free look config `freelook.cfg` (`enabled`, `mode`)

## Work State

### Completed
- **Motion blur removal**: source clean (zero references), `clean build` successful, deployed jar has zero `MotionBlur`/`motion_blur` entries, stale `motionblur.cfg` deleted from game dir
- **Free look implemented and deployed**: 47 headless state-machine checks pass (hold/toggle edge detection, master-switch gating, pitch clamp ±90° over 5000 frames, yaw wrap, decay convergence, frame-rate independence, config round-trip, malformed-input handling)
- **Keybind wiring verified**: 8 checks — present in `keyBindings` array (34 entries), no collision against vanilla defaults, category `key.categories.misc`, lang `key.freeLook`
- All hooks confirmed in bytecode via `javap -c -p` in correct methods; `FreeLook.load()` confirmed in `Minecraft.run()` at offset 22
- `clean build` → `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, 0 errors
- Deployed to `versions/GradleMCP-Base-1.8.9/GradleMCP-Base-1.8.9.jar`, 7161 entries, 10617.8 KB, `META-INF` stripped
- **Caught and fixed a bug in own third-person camera math**: folding offsets into `f1`/`f2` is wrong — that pair acts on the camera-offset vector and must be identity for the camera to land at `eye − viewDir·d3`; with offsets the camera would sit at body pitch **+2×** free-look pitch. Fixed by keeping `f1`/`f2` on body angles and adding separate `rayYaw`/`rayPitch` for the collision raytrace. Reasoning documented in a comment at the site
- Verified safe: `getLookVec()` is only called by `EntityFireball`; the player model renderer (`RendererLivingEntity` lines 125/155) reads `rotationYawHead`/`rotationPitch` fields directly, so body/head stay put
- Glide build stopped per user instruction; Glide repo left clean (only user's own `Glide.java` version bump)
- Earlier session work intact: `/fov`, `/bob`, always-sprint, `/fps` overlay + `fpsdisplay.cfg`, `/nhk`, plus non-mod fixes (`EntityLivingBase` jump cooldown, `Cartesian.java` cast fix, `build.gradle` `options.release = 8`, `Start.java` natives path)

### Active
(none)

### Blocked
- **No visual verification possible**: model has no image input; screenshots and user-attached PNGs come back unreadable. Runtime confirmation of bobbing, `/fov`, `/fps`, NoHurtCam, `/anim`, and `/mb` absence plus `/freelook` behaviour is on the user. Flagged that if free look lands somewhere unexpected, testing `thirdPersonView` 0 vs 1 vs 2 isolates camera math from anything else

### Resolved (previously blocked)
- Deploy was blocked by the running game holding the jar (PID 14740, file lock made `Move-Item` fail silently). Game has since closed; deploy succeeded. Must always verify the deployed jar after deploy — the first attempt read a stale file and would have falsely reported success

2. If asked to build Glide in future: `gradlew.bat build -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs="-Xmx3G -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=512m"` (verified to clear `:deobfMcMCP` OOM), requires `JAVA_HOME=C:\Users\dinhv\.jdks\azul-1.8.0_504`

- `FILE_NAME` in `Animations`/`FreeLook` is package-private so command javadoc `{@value}` resolves
- `Animations.isEnabled()` is the master gate folded into every accessor
- LWJGL key codes confirmed from existing vanilla defaults: `KEY_LSHIFT=42`, `KEY_LCONTROL=29`, `KEY_A=30`, `KEY_V=47`, `KEY_F2=60`, `KEY_F5=63`, `KEY_F11=87`

- `options.release = 8` in `build.gradle` is required, not just `sourceCompatibility`
- TLauncher regenerates the version manifest; manual JSON edits get clobbered
- Machine has only7.9 GB RAM total (~1.5 GB free)
- `_JAVA_OPTIONS` is set in the environment
- Animations + motion blur exist as **independent copies** in both codebases; future Glide-side changes will not reach GradleMCPBase

**New command surface**
```
/freelook view              → shows usage + current value
/freelook view first        → ignored in third person
```

**How the restriction is enforced** — two layers, because the two hooks refresh on different clocks:

1. `EntityPlayerSP.setAngles` → `onMouseLook` returns `false` in a disallowed view, so the raw deltas fall through to `super.setAngles` and turn the body normally. It also *drops* the offset outright rather than easing, so pressing F5 snaps the camera exactly where the body is instead of drifting home over ~90 ms.
2. `FreeLook.getYawOffset(boolean)` / `getPitchOffset(boolean)` — both `EntityRenderer.orientCamera` and `EntityPlayerSP.getLook` now read these instead of the raw `getYaw()`/`getPitch()`. The offsets only refresh once a tick but the camera draws every frame, so without this there'd be a one-frame window where a banned view still rendered a stale offset. Raw accessors stay unmasked for anything else that wants them.

Also cleared: `latched` is dropped on entering a disallowed view, so a TOGGLE can't stay latched off-screen and swing the camera when you F5 back. Config gains `view=` in `freelook.cfg`, and a pre-existing config with no `view` line leaves the default rather than landing on null.

messages.summary:
## Objective
Port Glide client mods into the MCP 1.8.9 base (GradleMCPBase) as command-driven settings, build, verify, and deploy to a TLauncher version directory. Motion blur was removed; free look with `/freelook mode <hold|toggle>` and an Options→Controls keybind exists; free look was then extended with a `/freelook view <first|third|both>` restriction.

## Requirements
- Convert features into plain MCP source; do NOT add Forge/Mixin/Essential frameworks
- **Standing rule: never launch the client after a build**
- **Standing rule: do NOT build the Glide client**
- Verify with `./gradlew build`; commit only when asked (never asked)
- Persistence via load/save/reset plus `.cfg` files
- Do not leave stray files in the Glide repo
- **Newest:** the built jar must remain in `./build/libs` after deploy

## Decisions
- `/anim`, `/freelook` consumed in `GuiScreen.sendChatMessage(String, boolean)` via `ClientCommands.handle()`
- Animations: 10 settings + master switch, all off by default; config `animations.cfg`
- Motion blur fully removed at user request ("motionblur is so broken, remove it plese") — including dead `ShaderGroup.getListShaders()`
- Free look intercepts `EntityPlayerSP.setAngles`; body rotation never mutated
- Only 3 hooks: `setAngles` (divert deltas), `EntityRenderer.orientCamera` (view offsets), `EntityPlayerSP.getLook` (offsets so crosshair/outline/block-breaking follow camera)
- Free look starts **enabled**; default bind **V (47)**
- `FreeLook.step(float,float,boolean)` is package-private for headless testing
- Third-person camera math: `f1`/`f2` must stay on body angles (identity for the rotate sandwich); folding offsets in put the camera at body pitch **+2×** free-look pitch. Fixed with separate `rayYaw`/`rayPitch` for the raytrace; documented in a comment at the site
- Free look view restriction implemented as a **separate setting** (`/freelook view`), not a `mode` value — user chose "Restrict where it works" over per-view settings and over folding into mode
- View gate enforced in **two layers**: `onMouseLook` returns false + drops offsets in a disallowed view; and new `getYawOffset(boolean)`/`getPitchOffset(boolean)` mask offsets per-view for the two render hooks (offsets refresh once/tick, camera draws every frame)
- `latched` dropped on entering a disallowed view so a TOGGLE can't swing the camera when F5 returns
- Deploy switched from `Move-Item` to `Copy-Item` so `build/libs` keeps its jar

## Work State

### Completed
- **Motion blur removal**: source clean, deployed jar has zero `MotionBlur`/`motion_blur` entries, stale `motionblur.cfg` deleted from game dir
- **Free look + keybind**: implemented, wired, deployed; previously 47 state-machine checks + 8 keybind checks
- **`/freelook view <first|third|both>`**: implemented, built, deployed. Accepts aliases `1`, `3`, `all`, and `perspective` as a subcommand alias. Defaults to `both` (preserves old behaviour). `view=` added to `freelook.cfg`; missing or junk `view` leaves the current value
- `FreeLookTest` expanded 47 → **83 checks**, all passing (truth table for BOTH/FIRST/THIRD, offset masking, view gate driven through the real `onMouseLook` using a `sun.misc.Unsafe`-allocated stand-in `Minecraft`, `view` config round-trip/rejection/missing-line)
- `KeyBindTest`: **8 checks** passing
- `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, 0 errors
- Bytecode verified: `getYawOffset`/`getPitchOffset` exist and are called from both `orientCamera` and `getLook`
- Deployed via `Copy-Item`; `build/libs` and version jar SHA-256 identical, 7166 entries
- Temp workspace wiped at one point; recreated with a `cp-init.gradle` `printCp` task generating `cp.txt` (34 entries, project classes dir now first — old shadowing gone)

### Active
(none)

### Blocked
- **No visual verification possible**: model has no image input; screenshots and user-attached PNGs come back unreadable. Runtime confirmation of bobbing, `/fov`, `/fps`, NoHurtCam, `/anim`, `/mb` absence, `/freelook` behaviour, and the new view restriction is on the user. Suggested check: `/freelook view third` in first person should do nothing until F5; F5 should hand the camera back instantly, not ease

### Resolved
- Deploy was blocked earlier by the running game holding the jar; now deploys with `Copy-Item` and verifies via SHA-256

## Next Move
1. Await user direction; nothing pending. Likely: commit the work (never committed)
2. If asked to build Glide: `gradlew.bat build -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs="-Xmx3G -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=512m"`, requires `JAVA_HOME=C:\Users\dinhv\.jdks\azul-1.8.0_504`

## Relevant Files
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/commands/FreeLook.java`: state machine, `View` enum (`BOTH`/`FIRST`/`THIRD`), `allowsView(boolean)`, `getYawOffset`/`getPitchOffset`, `allowsCurrentView()`, `dropIfDisallowed()`, `freelook.cfg`
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/commands/FreeLookCommand.java`: `/freelook` — status, `on|off`, `mode`, `view`, `reset`
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/entity/EntityPlayerSP.java`: `setAngles` + `getLook` overrides (~line 112-160); `getLook` now reads `thirdPersonView` and the view-aware accessors
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/renderer/EntityRenderer.java`: `orientCamera` (~line 659) — `thirdPersonView` local, `freeYaw`/`freePitch` from offset accessors; third-person `f1`/`f2` + `rayYaw`/`rayPitch` at ~709-723

## Objective
Port Glide client mods into the MCP 1.8.9 base (GradleMCPBase) as command-driven settings. Current task: add an in-game GUI to configure all mods, and consolidate all mod settings into exactly one `.cfg` file.

## Requirements
- Convert features into plain MCP source; do NOT add Forge/Mixin/Essential frameworks
- **Standing rule: never launch the client after a build**
- **Standing rule: do NOT build the Glide client**
- Verify with `./gradlew build`; commit only when asked (never asked)
- Persistence via load/save/reset plus `.cfg` files
- Do not leave stray files in the Glide repo
- Built jar must remain in `./build/libs` after deploy
- Exactly **one** `.cfg` file holds all mod settings

## Decisions
- `/anim`, `/freelook`, `/config` consumed in `GuiScreen.sendChatMessage(String, boolean)` via `ClientCommands.handle()`
- Animations: 10 settings + master switch, all off by default
- Motion blur fully removed (including dead `ShaderGroup.getListShaders()`)
- Free look: 3 hooks only — `EntityPlayerSP.setAngles` (divert deltas), `EntityRenderer.orientCamera` (view offsets), `EntityPlayerSP.getLook` (offsets); third-person camera uses separate `rayYaw`/`rayPitch`
- Free look view restriction is a separate setting (`/freelook view <first|third|both>`), defaults to `both`, free look starts enabled, default bind V (47)
- **Single cfg scope (user chose)**: all 7 mods in `client.cfg`; the four options.txt-backed ones (fov, bob, nhk, sprint) are mirrored in and re-applied to `GameSettings` at startup; `GameSettings.saveOptions()` calls `ClientConfig.saveVanilla()` so vanilla Options changes fold back in
- **GUI open routes (user chose)**: `/config` command + new keybind in Options→Controls (unbound default) + button on the pause menu
- **Old cfg files (user chose)**: migrate/fold in on first run, then keep them on disk as backups (do NOT delete)
- GUI design: `GuiClientSettings extends GuiScreen` with a `GuiListExtended` (rows implement `IGuiListEntry`), vanilla-style full-width buttons "Label: Value" and `GuiSlider`s; sub-settings greyed out via `enabled=false` when their master switch is off; sections as headers; bottom buttons Done + Reset All
- fps `colour` is a CHOICE over 8 presets in the GUI (`/fps color <hex>` stays the precise tool); row gated on `fps.autoColour`
- `ClientConfig` lives in `net.minecraft.client.commands` (same package as the mods so it can reach package-private statics); GUI in `net.minecraft.client.gui`
- File format: `[section]` headers with `key=value` lines; sections written in the same order as the settings table
- Mods keep their own statics/accessors (no refactor of verified code); only persistence is delegated
- Re-entrancy guard `ClientConfig.loading` so per-key setters during load don't each write the file
- File is written on load too, so `client.cfg` is always complete
- `Animations.setSmoothSneakSpeed` now clamps (clamping moved out of the deleted `applySetting`)
- `FpsOverlay.setColourOnly(int)` / `setAutoColour(boolean)` added package-private so load can apply `autoColour` and `colour` independently (avoids the bug the old `seen.colour && !seen.autoColour` fixup guarded)
- Deploy switched from `Move-Item` to `Copy-Item` so `build/libs` keeps its jar

## What was added

**One config file — `client.cfg`**
`ClientConfig.java` is now the single persistence point for all 7 mods. It holds a settings table (28 rows across `[fov] [bob] [nhk] [sprint] [animations] [fps] [freelook]`) where each row names its own getter/setter, so each mod's existing validation and clamping is reused rather than reimplemented. `Animations`/`FreeLook`/`FpsOverlay` keep their own statics and accessors — only file I/O was delegated away.

- `load()` resets to defaults, parses, migrates the old per-mod files if `client.cfg` is absent, then rewrites the file so it's always complete.
- Writes are suppressed before the first `load()` — otherwise an early `GameSettings.saveOptions()` would leave a complete-looking `client.cfg` and the legacy import would never run.
- `GameSettings.saveOptions()` calls `saveVanilla()` at the end, so moving a slider in vanilla Options folds back into `client.cfg` instead of being reverted next launch.

**The GUI — `GuiClientSettings`**
Built from `ClientConfig.settings()`, so a setting only has to be registered once. Sections are gold headers; toggles and choices are cycling buttons, numbers are `GuiSlider`s, and a row whose master switch is off is greyed out. Two things needed working around in this build: `GuiSlider.mouseDragged` is protected and `GuiScreen.mouseClickMove` is empty, so `DragSlider` widens the override and the screen forwards drags itself; and slider drags report a value per pixel, so writes are held via `beginBulkChange()`/`endBulkChange()` and flushed once on release.
