- **Legacy migration never ran.** `parse()` did `sections.get("")` for headerless files, which returned `null` on an empty map, so every key was skipped. Now the `""` bucket is created up front.
- **The FPS colour row was gated backwards.** `autoColour` was registered as its master with normal gate semantics, greying the row out exactly when the colour *was* live. Added `invertGate` — that row now greys out while colour-by-FPS is on, which is when it has no effect.

options.label: Third-back on, restore prior view on off (Recommended)
options.description: Engaging free look switches the camera to third person (behind). Releasing it puts the camera back to whatever view you were in before - first person, or front-facing third person if that's where you were.

options.label: Third-back on, always return to first person

messages.summary:
## Objective
Port Glide client mods into the MCP 1.8.9 base (GradleMCPBase) as command-driven settings. Task complete: added an in-game GUI to configure all mods and consolidated all mod settings into exactly one `.cfg` file (`client.cfg`).

## Requirements
- Convert features into plain MCP source; do NOT add Forge/Mixin/Essential frameworks
- **Standing rule: never launch the client after a build**
- **Standing rule: do NOT build the Glide client**
- Verify with `./gradlew build`; commit only when asked (never asked)
- Persistence via load/save/reset plus `.cfg` files
- Do not leave stray files in the Glide repo
- Built jar must remain in `./build/libs` after deploy
- Exactly **one** `.cfg` file holds all mod settings

## Decisions
- GUI open routes: `/config` command (aliases `/settings`, `/mods`), new unbound keybind in Options→Controls, pause-menu button
- `GuiClientSettings extends GuiScreen` with a custom `GuiSlot`; vanilla-style full-width "Label: Value" cycling buttons for TOGGLE/CHOICE, `GuiSlider`s for SLIDER; sub-settings greyed via `enabled=false` when master off; gold section headers; Done + Reset All at bottom; `client.cfg` filename hint- fps `colour` is a CHOICE over 8 presets (gate on `fps.autoColour`); `/fps color <hex>` stays the precise tool
- `ClientConfig` lives in `net.minecraft.client.commands` (same package as mods); GUI in `net.minecraft.client.gui`
- Single cfg scope (user chose): all 7 mods in `client.cfg`; the four options.txt-backed ones (fov, bob, nhk, sprint) mirrored in and re-applied to `GameSettings`; `GameSettings.saveOptions()` calls `ClientConfig.saveVanilla()`
- Old cfg files: migrate/fold in on first run only (when `client.cfg` absent), then keep on disk as backups
- File format `[section]` headers + `key=value`, sections in settings-table order
- Mods keep their own statics/accessors; only persistence delegated
- Guards: `loading` (no write per key during load), `deferring`/`pending` (`beginBulkChange`/`endBulkChange` so a slider drag costs one write), `loaded` (refuse writes before first load so migration isn't pre-empted)
- Unknown/unreadable value on load → falls back to the **default** (load resets first), not last-known-good
- File written on load too, so `client.cfg` is always complete
- `ClientConfig.setFov` writes `settings.fovSetting` directly rather than through `GameSettings.Options.FOV` (equivalent, avoids enum clinit)
- `ClientCommand.getAliases()` added as a Java 8 `default` method (empty by default)
- FPS colour/autoColour kept independent in the table; `load()` has `fixFpsColourPair()` to honour a `colour`-without-`autoColour` file
- Deploy uses `Copy-Item` so `build/libs` keeps its jar, verified by SHA-256

## Work State
### Completed
- Motion blur removal, free look + keybind, `/freelook view` (from prior session)
- `ClientConfig.java` (1209 lines): settings table (`Kind` TOGGLE/CHOICE/SLIDER; `Setting` with section/key/label/choices/min/max/integral/getter/setter/master gate/`invertGate`), `BY_KEY` index, `settings()`, `sectionTitle()`, `getConfigFile()`, `load()`, `migrate()`/`copyLegacy()`, section-aware `parse()`, `save()`, `beginBulkChange()`/`endBulkChange()`, `write()`, `saveVanilla()`, `resetAll()`
- `Animations.java`, `FreeLook.java`, `FpsOverlay.java` rewritten to delegate persistence; `resetToDefaults()` package-private; `FpsOverlay.setColourOnly(int)`/`setAutoColour(boolean)` added
- `GuiClientSettings.java` (new, ~450 lines) with inner `Row`, `DragSlider` (widens `mouseDragged` to public), `SliderResponder`, `SliderFormatter`, `SettingsList extends GuiSlot`

## What was added

**`freelook.autoF5`** (default off) — engaging free look moves the camera behind the player; releasing hands it back to first person.

- `FreeLook.java`: `isAutoF5()` / `setAutoF5(boolean)`, hooked to the engage/release edge in `step()`
- `FreeLookCommand.java`: `/freelook f5 <on|off>` (alias `autof5`), shown in the `/freelook` status line
- `ClientConfig.java`: one table row, so it persists in `client.cfg` and appears in the `/config` GUI automatically

## Design points worth knowing

- **Edge-triggered only.** It fires on the transition of `active`, never while free look is being held — so pressing F5 yourself while free looking is never fought.
- **View restriction stays authoritative.** `view=first` leaves auto-F5 inert rather than quietly overriding it, and `/freelook f5 on` says so in chat instead of appearing broken.
- **It only hands back a camera it moved.** An `autoF5Held` flag means a player already in third person doesn't get dragged to first person when free look ends or the switch is turned off.

## Three bugs found and fixed while building this

1. **Stranded camera on reset** — `resetToDefaults()` cleared `autoF5Held` without releasing, leaving the camera in third person with nothing tracking it. Now releases first.
2. **Stranded camera on `/freelook off`** — `setEnabled(false)` drops offsets immediately rather than waiting for the next tick's engage edge, so it now releases too.
3. **Stranded camera on `/freelook view first`** — restricting away from third person has to give the camera back, since auto-F5 can't act in first person.

## Verification

- `./gradlew build` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- `ConfigTest` 239/239 (was 235; the new row gets table-driven round-trip coverage automatically)
- `FreeLookTest` 106/106 (was 84; 22 new checks)

The command warns you when you enable that combination, but if it annoys you in practice the fix is to release to the *previous* view instead of always first person.

## What it does

`/reachcircle` (alias `/reach`) — draws a ring on the ground at your feet, 3 blocks radius. Also toggleable via `/reachcircle on|off`, `/reachcircle reset`, the `/config` GUI (new "Reach circle" section), or `Reset All`.

## Files

- `commands/ReachCircle.java` — new mod: state, rendering, delegated persistence
- `commands/ReachCircleCommand.java` — new `/reachcircle` command
- `ClientConfig.java` — `reachcircle` section, table row, reset wiring
- `ClientCommands.java` — registration
- `EntityRenderer.java` — render hook

## Rendering approach

Two things drove the design:

**Where to draw.** Hooked at the `ForgeHooksClient_dispatchRenderLast` spot in `renderWorldPass` — the exact equivalent of Forge's `RenderWorldLastEvent`. That's after terrain, entities and particles are done, so the ring sits *over* the world and stays occluded by walls rather than drawing through them. It runs on every pass, which is what anaglyph needs (each pass has its own colour mask, so it lands in both eyes).

**Why not a line loop.** I drew it as a flat annulus (triangle strip, 96 segments) rather than `GL_LINES`. A one-pixel line on the ground shimmers badly as the camera turns, and drivers are free to clamp line width to 1.0 anyway — vanilla's own selection box uses `glLineWidth(2.0F)` and gets away with it because it sits on a box edge, not a ground plane. The band has a real width (0.1 blocks), so it reads the same from any angle for the same cost. Culling is disabled since the winding is inside-out by construction.

## One thing you should know

I used a literal `RADIUS = 3.0F` as you asked, **not** `playerController.getBlockReachDistance()`. In this build that method returns **4.5** in survival and 5.0 in creative, not 3 — it measures from the eye, not the feet. So driving the circle from it would have produced a 4.5-block ring, which isn't what you asked for.

The tradeoff: a 3-block ring understates your actual4.5 survival reach. If you'd rather it track real reach, it's a one-line change to `ReachCircle.RADIUS`, or I can add a radius slider — say the word.

Done. The position HUD is built, tested, and deployed.

## What it shows

```
XYZ: 1.5000000000 / -2.2500000000 / 3.1250000000
Yaw: 90.5000000000  Pitch: -12.5000000000
```

All five values at 10 decimals. `/coords` (aliases `/xyz`, `/position`) — `on|off`, `size <0.5-3>`, `pos <x> <y>`, `reset`. Also in the `/config` GUI as a "Position HUD" section. Defaults to off, positioned at (4, 14) so it doesn't collide with the FPS readout at (4, 4).

## Read this before you judge the precision

**The 10 decimals are real for XYZ, but not for yaw/pitch.** The underlying fields differ:

- `Entity.posX/posY/posZ` are **doubles** → at ordinary coordinates they resolve far finer than 1e-10. Those digits are genuine.
- `rotationYaw`/`rotationPitch` are **floats** → ~7 significant decimal digits. A yaw near 180 has a resolution around 1.5e-5, so past roughly the 5th decimal you're reading the float's rounding, not the game state.

I chose to print 10 decimals anyway rather than truncate. `0.1f` widens to `0.10000000149011612`, so the HUD shows `0.1000000015` — that's the float's actual granularity, which is more informative than a shorter number that looks precise. There's a test pinning both behaviours so it can't quietly change.

Getting real 1e-10 yaw would mean storing angles as doubles throughout `Entity`, which is well outside this task. If you want it, that's a real (and invasive) change — say so and I'll scope it.

Two smaller decisions: values are **raw, not interpolated**, so they step at the tick rate and match the server's view (same as vanilla F3); and yaw is folded into a single turn, since Minecraft lets it grow unbounded.

## Objective
Port Glide client mods into the MCP 1.8.9 base (GradleMCPBase) as command-driven settings, with all settings in one `.cfg` file. Three features added this session: auto-F5 third-person for free look, a `ReachCircle` ground ring mod, and a high-precision X/Y/Z + yaw/pitch position HUD.

## Requirements
- Plain MCP source; no Forge/Mixin/Essential frameworks
- **Standing rule: never launch the client after a build**
- **Standing rule: do NOT build the Glide client**
- Verify with `./gradlew build`; commit only when asked (never asked — nothing committed)
- Persistence via load/save/reset plus `.cfg` files; exactly **one** `.cfg` holds all settings
- Built jar must remain in `./build/libs` after deploy
- Do not leave stray files in the Glide repo
- New mods should follow the established pattern: own command + config section + GUI row

## Decisions
- **Auto-F5** (user answered2 questions): engaging free look → third-person-back; releasing → **always** first person (not restore prior view). Inert when `view=first`, because auto-F5 and "never in third person" cannot both be honoured; the restriction stays authoritative and the command says so in chat.
- Auto-F5 fires only on the **engage/release edge** in `step()`, never while held, so pressing F5 manually is never fought.
- Added `autoF5Held` flag: only the switch that moved the camera may move it back. Without it, releasing would drag an already-third-person player to first person.
- **ReachCircle radius hardcoded to 3.0F**, *not* `playerController.getBlockReachDistance()` — in this build that returns 4.5 survival / 5.0 creative (measured from eye, not feet), contradicting the requested3 blocks.
- ReachCircle drawn as a **flat annulus (triangle strip, 96 segments)**, not a line loop: ground-level 1px lines shimmer and drivers clamp line width. Cull disabled since winding is inside-out by construction.
- ReachCircle hooked at the `Reflector.ForgeHooksClient_dispatchRenderLast` spot in `EntityRenderer.renderWorldPass` (= Forge `RenderWorldLastEvent`), so it draws over the world and stays occluded. Runs on every pass, which is what anaglyph needs.
- **Position HUD precision**: print 10 decimals regardless of source precision. XYZ are `double` (genuine 1e-10); yaw/pitch are `float` (~7 significant digits), so the readout shows the float's real granularity rather than hiding it.
- HUD values are **raw, not interpolated** (step at tick rate, match server view, same as vanilla F3). Yaw is **folded to a single turn** since Minecraft lets it grow unbounded.
- `CoordsHud.number()` passes `Locale.ROOT` — mandatory, else comma locales render `1,5000000000` and three coords look like one field.
- HUD named `CoordsHud` (user did not name it); section `coords`, title "Position HUD"; defaults off, pos (4,14) to avoid the FPS readout at (4,4).
- Mods keep their own statics/accessors; only persistence delegated to `ClientConfig`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Auto-F5: `FreeLook.isAutoF5()/setAutoF5()`, `/freelook f5 <on|off>` (alias `autof5`), `freelook.autoF5` config row, status-line entry- Three auto-F5 stranded-camera bugs found and fixed: `resetToDefaults()`, `setEnabled(false)`, and `setView(View.FIRST)` all cleared/held state without handing the camera back
- `ReachCircle.java` + `ReachCircleCommand.java` (`/reachcircle`, alias `reach`, `reset`), config section/row, registry, `EntityRenderer` hook
- Fixed latent `ClientConfig.isMasterOn` fall-through trap (returned `FreeLook.isEnabled()` for unknown sections) — extended for both `reachcircle` and `coords`
- `CoordsHud.java` + `CoordsCommand.java` (`/coords`, aliases `xyz`/`position`, `size`, `pos`, `reset`), 4 config rows, registry, `GuiIngame` hook
- All harnesses pass: `CoordsHudTest` 69, `ConfigTest` 266, `ReachCircleTest` 22, `KeyBindTest` 15, `FreeLookTest` 106
- Mutation-tested two guards: removing `Locale.ROOT` → 8 failures with `1,5000000000`; reverting `isMasterOn` → 2 row failures
- Deployed each change, hash-verified, jar retained in `build/libs`, no stray files

### Active
- (none) — the last requested feature is complete and deployed

### Blocked
- **No visual verification possible**: model has no image input. Runtime confirmation of the HUD (does 10 decimals at size 1.0 fit the user's GUI scale — first line is ~57 chars wide), the reach circle's look/thickness, and all prior features is on the user.
- The Glide repo was not found on this machine (searched `C:\` to depth 3).

## Next Move
1. Ask the user to launch and confirm the position HUD (`/coords`), ReachCircle (`/reachcircle`), and auto-F5 (`/freelook f5 on`)
2. Fix anything they report visually
3. Commit only when asked

## Relevant Files

```java
/**
 * Folds the banked offset into the player's real rotation, so the body turns to face where the
 * free look camera was pointing.
 *
 * <p>Every consumer of the look vector adds {@link #getYawOffset} on top of a body field, and the

 * current and previous fields are therefore shifted by the same amount: the effective view vector
 * is unchanged, so the camera does not move at all, and the body simply arrives at the place the
 * offset was already describing.
 *
 * <p>Yaw, pitch and head yaw are all shifted, because the camera reads {@code rotationYaw} while
 * {@link net.minecraft.entity.EntityLivingBase#getLook} reads {@code rotationYawHead}; leaving
 * either behind would split the two apart by the offset.
 *
 * @return true if an offset was committed
 */
public static boolean commitTo(EntityLivingBase player)
{
    if (player == null)
    {
        return false;
    }

    float commitYaw;
    float commitPitch;

    if (yaw != 0.0F || pitch != 0.0F)

    player.prevRotationYaw += commitYaw;
    player.rotationPitch = clampPitch(player.rotationPitch + commitPitch);
    player.prevRotationPitch += commitPitch;
    player.rotationYawHead = wrapDegrees(player.rotationYawHead + commitYaw);
    player.prevRotationYawHead += commitYaw;

    clearOffsets();
    lastYaw = 0.0F;
    lastPitch = 0.0F;
    return true;
}
```

Done. `ChangeRealLookVector` is in as **`/lookvector`** (aliases `realvector`, `commitlook`).

## What it does

Free look deliberately never touches your body — that's what keeps walking, sprinting and the player model honest while you aim sideways. This mod hands the banked offset over, so the body turns to face where the camera was pointing. Everything that reads the real rotation (attack direction, the packets the server checks, your rendered model) then agrees with where you're actually looking.

## One thing I had to work around

You picked the chat command, and I warned you it might not work. Checking rather than assuming, it's **worse than I said**: opening chat does *not* stop free look (`inGameHasFocus` is window focus, not GUI state), so the offset survives — but hold mode eases it away with a **90 ms** time constant the instant you release the key. You cannot type a command that fast, so a literal implementation would have applied nothing in hold mode.

So FreeLook now remembers the offset from the last engaged frame (`lastYaw`/`lastPitch`) and the commit falls back to it. Hold mode applies the direction the camera was last pointing; toggle mode applies the live offset directly. Same number, just read a moment later. It's cleared on disable, reset and view changes, since those mean you're genuinely no longer pointing that way.

## Correctness

I found vanilla's own idiom for this — `Entity.setAngles` (Entity.java:247) clamps the current field, *then* moves `prevRotation*` by the actual resulting delta. The commit mirrors it exactly, on all three fields (`rotationYaw`, `rotationPitch`, `rotationYawHead`). Head yaw matters because the camera reads `rotationYaw` while `getLook` reads `rotationYawHead`; miss either and the crosshair stops matching the camera.

`LookVectorTest` recomputes the camera and look-vector bases before and after a commit at five interpolation factors and requires them to agree. **82 checks.** I mutation-tested all seven guards — dropping any single `prevRotation*` shift, the pitch clamp, or either `last*` recording each produces a distinct failure.

All other harnesses still pass: ConfigTest 272, CoordsHudTest 69, ReachCircleTest 22, KeyBindTest 15. FreeLookTest has its one pre-existing `Thread.sleep(60)` wall-clock flake (varying 0.44/0.46 decay on reruns, in untouched easing code).

Config: `[lookvector] enabled`, **default on** — it's an explicitly-typed command with no passive behaviour, so "I typed it and it said disabled" seemed the worse first experience. 35 settings across 10 sections. Nothing committed.

**Worth your eyes:** `/lookvector` while holding free look, and check `/freelook`'s new hint line appears. I can't see the game, so the visual no-jump guarantee is proven numerically but not by eye.

## Requirements
- Plain MCP source; no Forge/Mixin/Essential frameworks
- **Standing rule: never launch the client after a build**

- **Trigger: chat command** `/lookvector` (aliases `realvector`, `commitlook`), per user

- Pitch clamp means the view settles at ±90 for the part the body can't hold — this is vanilla's own behaviour, not a defect.
- Mod named `LookVector`, section `lookvector`, title "Real look vector"; **defaults ON** (unlike display mods) since the only way to trigger it is typing the command.

```java
private static Timer bareTimer() throws Exception

}
```

## Objective
Port Glide client mods into the MCP 1.8.9 base (GradleMCPBase) as command-driven settings, all in one `.cfg`. This session adds two mods: `TickSpeed` (client-side tick speed) and `JumpDelay` (adjustable jump delay).

## Requirements
- Plain MCP source; no Forge/Mixin/Essential frameworks
- **Standing rule: never launch the client after a build**
- **Standing rule: do NOT build the Glide client**
- Verify with `./gradlew build`; commit only when asked (never asked — nothing committed)
- Persistence via load/save/reset plus `.cfg` files; exactly **one** `.cfg` holds all settings
- Built jar must remain in `./build/libs` after deploy
- Do not leave stray files in the Glide repo
- New mods follow the established pattern: own command + config section + GUI row

## Decisions
- **TickSpeed = "input speed only, no desync"** (user's choice): raise client tick rate for input/GUI/key polling, but hold world + sound + particle work to exactly 20/s so nothing outruns the 20 TPS server.
- **JumpDelay = cooldown after each jump while space is held** (user: "when hold space key, there is a delay before the new jump, the delay options can ajust that delay"), **measured in ticks**.
- Vanilla 1.8.9 already has this: `EntityLivingBase.jumpTicks = 10` (decremented at L1686-1689, gated at L1754, reset to 0 at L1762 when jump is released) — a cooldown that exists only while the key is held. A previous session already patched `10` → `0`. The mod restores it as a configurable value.
- World tick split uses a **carried credit accumulator** (`credit += BASE/ticks`, emit when `credit >= 1`) so any rate lands on exactly 20 world ticks/s with no drift; short-circuits to `true` when disabled or `ticks <= BASE` (below base the world runs at the input rate = slow motion).
- Must gate `mcSoundHandler.update()` too: `SoundManager.updateAllSounds()` L196 does `++playTime` and `itickablesound.update()`, so ungated sounds would play N× fast and finish N× sooner. Same for `effectRenderer.updateEffects()`, `theWorld.tick()`, `renderGlobal.updateClouds()`, the lightning-bolt counter, `entityRenderer.updateRenderer()`.
- `Timer.ticksPerSecond` made `public` (consistent with sibling `timerSpeed`).
- Server never simulates walking jumps — `C0CPacketInput` is sent only while riding (EntityPlayerSP L164-168) and `EntityPlayerMP.setEntityActionState` only applies when `ridingEntity != null`, so the client position packets are authoritative and a client-only delay needs no packet gating (except riding, gated anyway for consistency).
- JumpDelay arms via an **override of `EntityPlayer.jump()`** (public, EntityPlayerSP-overridable) rather than predicting the jump — exact semantics. `advance()` runs before `allowJump()` so the delay is exact (matches vanilla's 10-tick gap).
- Ranges: TickSpeed `MIN_TICKS=5`, `MAX_TICKS=200`, default20, enabled default **false**. JumpDelay 0–20 ticks, default **0**, enabled default **true** (inert until configured).
- Two new config sections `tickspeed` and `jumpdelay`; two new commands registered in `ClientCommands`.

## Work State
### Completed
- `LookVector` / `/lookvector` from the previous session (built, deployed, SHA256-verified, 82-check harness, 7 mutations verified) — all uncommitted.

### Active
- **TickSpeed**: `TickSpeed.java` written; `Timer.ticksPerSecond` made public; first hook inserted into `Minecraft.runGameLoop`.
  - **Outstanding bug**: `TickSpeed.applyTo(this.timer)` was inserted only inside the `if (this.isGamePaused && this.theWorld != null)` branch, so the normal `else { this.timer.updateTimer(); }` path never applies the tick speed. It must run before the `if` at Minecraft.java:992 (or in both branches).
  - **Outstanding**: the `runTick` world gate. Add `final boolean worldTick = !this.isGamePaused && TickSpeed.isWorldTick();` just before Minecraft.java:2067 (`if (this.theWorld != null)`), then swap the 7 `!this.isGamePaused` conditions at L2082, 2089, 2096, 2111, 2119, 2147, 2154 to `worldTick`. Declared before L2067 so it is in scope at L2111 (outside the `theWorld != null` block).
- **JumpDelay**: design settled, no code written yet.

### Blocked
- **No visual verification possible** — model has no image input; runtime confirmation is on the user.
- Glide repo not found on this machine (searched `C:\` to depth 3).

## Next Move
1. Fix the `applyTo` placement so the non-paused path applies the tick speed (move it above the `if (this.isGamePaused...)` block at Minecraft.java:992).
2. Add the `worldTick` local + 7 condition swaps in `Minecraft.runTick()`.
3. Write `JumpDelay.java` and wire the three `EntityPlayerSP` hooks: `updateEntityActionState()` L620, a `jump()` override, and the riding packet at L167.
4. Add `SECTION_TICKSPEED`/`SECTION_JUMPDELAY` to `ClientConfig` (constants, settings, `masterToggle` setter/getter, `isMasterOn`, `sectionTitle`, `load()`, `resetAll()`) and update `EXPECTED_SETTINGS`/section count in ConfigTest.
5. Write `TickSpeedCommand` and `JumpDelayCommand`; register both in `ClientCommands`.
6. Add test harnesses (`TickSpeedTest`, `JumpDelayTest`) plus ConfigTest updates; verify with mutation sweeps (drop the accumulator carry, drop `jumpTicks` arming, drop the sound gate, etc.).
7. `./gradlew build`, deploy, SHA256-verify, retain jar in `build/libs`, no stray files.
8. Ask the user to launch and confirm; commit only when asked.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/commands/TickSpeed.java`: new mod, written; `isWorldTick()` accumulator, `applyTo(Timer)`, `reachable()`/`unreachable()` FPS-ceiling reporting, `trim()`
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/util/Timer.java`: `ticksPerSecond` now public; L59 `elapsedPartialTicks += d2 * timerSpeed * ticksPerSecond`; L63 clamps `elapsedTicks` to 10
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/Minecraft.java`: `runGameLoop` L982 (hook misplaced in paused branch), L1017 `for (int j = 0; j < this.timer.elapsedTicks; ++j) this.runTick()`, `runTick` L2067-2157 (7 gates), L2189-2190 `startServerThread()`
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/entity/EntityPlayerSP.java`: L167 riding packet, L499 `isServerWorld()` returns true, L612-626 `updateEntityActionState()` (L620 `isJumping = movementInput.jump`)
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/entity/EntityLivingBase.java`: L111 `jumpTicks`, L1686-1689 decrement, L1737 `updateEntityActionState()`, L1744 gate, L1754-1757 `jump()` + `jumpTicks = 0` (was `10`), L1762 reset
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/entity/player/EntityPlayer.java`: L1557 `public void jump()` — the override point
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/audio/SoundManager.java`: L194-196 `updateAllSounds()` / `++playTime` — why sound must be gated
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/commands/ClientConfig.java`: config wiring
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/commands/ClientCommands.java`: command registry
- `src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/commands/LookVector.java`, `LookVectorCommand.java`: previous feature, the pattern to copy
- `C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\ConfigTest.java`: `EXPECTED_SETTINGS = 35`, 10 sections ending `lookvector` — must be updated
- `C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\LookVectorTest.java`: 82-check harness pattern to copy
- `C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\cp.txt`: runtime classpath
- `C:\Users\dinhv\AppData\Roaming\.tlauncher\legacy\Minecraft\game\versions\GradleMCP-Base-1.8.9`: deploy target (jar in version **root**, no `mods` folder)

## Important Context
- **Everything remains uncommitted** in GradleMCPBase; nothing committed or pushed.
- Build: `cd C:\Users\dinhv\IdeaProjects\GradleMCPBase; ./gradlew build` (use `;`, not `&&`). "Exited with code 1" from the wrapper is not a failure — trust `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`.
- **mtime trap**: restoring from a `.bak` via `Copy-Item`/`Move-Item` yields a stale mtime and Gradle reports `UP-TO-DATE` with mutated classes still in place. Always follow a restore with `./gradlew build --rerun-tasks` and confirm with a string search.
- `ClientConfig.save()` is a no-op until `load()` has run (`loading || !loaded`) — harnesses asserting on a written file must call `ClientConfig.load()` first.
- `GameSettings.Options.<clinit>` → `UnsatisfiedLinkError: no lwjgl64`. Never touch it headless; a plain `new GameSettings()` is fine.
- Harness pattern: `javac -nowarn -d <out> -cp <cp.txt> <Test>.java` then `java -cp "<out>;<cp>" <pkg>.<Test>`, cwd = temp dir. `sun.misc.Unsafe.allocateInstance` for stand-in `Minecraft`/`EntityPlayerSP`; `mcDataDir` is `public final` but reflection CAN set a non-static final field.
- `FreeLookTest`'s `easeBackToZero` is flaky (`Thread.sleep(60L)` on Windows sleeps ~70 ms). Pre-existing, in untouched code.
- `FreeLook.setEnabled(x)` calls `clearOffsets()`, so a toggle in tests discards any banked offset.
- Verify `ClientConfig.getConfigFile()` and `ClientConfig.FILE_NAME` exist as referenced by `TickSpeed.java`'s javadoc/helpers.
- Mods so far: fov, bob, nhk, sprint, animations, fps, freelook, reachcircle, coords, lookvector — 35 settings across 10 sections in `client.cfg`; tickspeed and jumpdelay make 12 sections.
- Animations + motion blur exist as **independent copies** in both codebases; Glide-side changes will not reach GradleMCPBase.

Both mods are built, tested, and deployed. Here's where things landed.

## What shipped

**`/tickspeed <5-200>`** — raises the client's own tick rate. Input polling, mouse and GUI run at the raised rate; physics, movement packets, sound, particles and the lightning counter are held to exactly 20/s by a single `worldTick` flag in `runTick()`. A carried credit accumulator (`credit += 20/ticks`, emit at `>= 1`) means any rate lands on 20 world ticks/s with no drift. At or below 20 it short-circuits, so a normal game is byte-identical to vanilla.

**`/jumpdelay <0-20>`** — gap between jumps while space is held, in ticks. Armed off the jump that actually happened (via an `EntityPlayerSP.jump()` override), so holding jump mid-air doesn't burn a gap you never used. The countdown runs down regardless of the key, so tapping doesn't hand back free jumps.

Both wired into `client.cfg` as sections 11 and 12 — 39 settings, 12 sections, one file.

## Two things worth flagging

**A real bug the harness caught.** My first `allowsJump()` recomputed `cooldown == 0`, but `step()` decrements *before* testing. On the tick the cooldown reached zero the two disagree — the counter reads clear while this tick's jump was refused. That is fed straight into `C0CPacketInput`, so the server would jump a horse on a tick the client had just blocked. Fixed by recording `step()`'s decision and answering from that.

**An equivalent mutant.** Mutating the accumulator threshold from `1.0` to `0.9` or `2.0` passed all 189 checks. That's not a gap: credit is allowed to go negative, so the threshold shifts the emission phase without changing the steady-state rate. I confirmed it with a standalone probe across nine rates. Noting it rather than chasing it.

189 checks in `TickJumpTest`, all passing. The harness also reads `Minecraft.java` and `EntityPlayerSP.java` at source level, because the runTick split can't be exercised headless — that's the part most likely to rot silently.
